https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Chemical Model of Raritan River Sediment for Lead Sensor System
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: In collaboration with the Environmental Science department at Rutgers University and the Center for Advanced Infrastructure and Technology (CAIT) this project seeks to develop a fast-acting sensor system and MINTEQ model program capable of producing a total Pb concentration from “fresh” sediment on the order of minutes. Pb concentrations in various chemical fractions of Raritan River sediment and environmental data was used to optimize a sediment geochemical model in MINTEQ. The MINTEQ geochemical model is used to determine the environmental conditions at various river sites that influence the fractions of lead bound to: dissolved organic matter (DOM), sulfide, carbonates, and hydrated ferrous oxide (HFO), an important fraction in the Raritan River. The MINTEQ model calibrated at a pH of 7.4 generates Pb 2+ fractions of 11.805% bound to DOM, 65.172% bound to sulfide, 0.677% bound to carbonate, and 19.816% bound to HFO similar to those seen in field samples. In a pH sweep of the model from 6.4 to 8.4, the Pb fraction bound to sulfides decreases while the fraction bound to HFO and DOM increased. A Cl sweep from 0.03 to 0.5M, indicates that additional Pb-Cl species form in higher concentrations of Cl with the fractions of each species increasing with Cl. The effect of HFO concentration was tested in a sweep from 0.00036 to 0.00056 g/L increasing the Pb fraction bound to HFO and decreasing the fractions bound to sulfide. These initial results indicate a MINTEQ model can improve our Pb speciation model from laboratory measurements in atypical chemical conditions when it errors significantly from total sediment Pb concentrations and provide data of Pb partitioning from sites not accessible by boat. Our sensor system and geochemical model opens the opportunity for accurate on-site Pb measurements and the potential to measure sediment Pb concentrations of an entire watershed within days. This point-of-use technology has the potential to quickly identify Pb contaminated areas for remediation and augment treatment processes for Pb in polluted sediment.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Systematic Exploration of Peg-Grafted Polyelectrolytes for Intracellular Drug Delivery
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The cellular and endosomal membranes represent a significant delivery barrier in cytosolically active therapeutics. To address this challenge, several investigators have developed cationic and pH-responsive self-assembling polymeric nanoparticles as a drug delivery vehicle to enhance cellular uptake and endosomal escape of drug cargoes into the cytosol. To date, these approaches have largely leveraged homopolymers or block copolymer architectures – as such, design rules for other polymer architectures remain poorly characterized. For this project, we fill that gap with exploration of a PEG-grafted copolymer system. Libraries of poly[poly(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate-co-butyl methacrylate-co-(2-diethylamino) ethyl methacrylate] (PEGMA-co-EB) graft copolymers with varying hydrophobic molecular weight, hydrophilic volume fraction and graft lengths was synthesized and characterized. They were then screened for hydrodynamic sizes, endosomolytic activity and drug delivery competency in vitro . Promising formulations were applied in a murine B16.F10 melanoma utilizing 2’4’-cGAMP, a STING agonist, as the therapeutic agent and cargo. From our in vitro experiments, we discovered that formulations with low hydrophilic volume fraction (W PEG ~ 20%), moderate hydrophobic molecular weight (MW ~ 30 kDa), and short graft lengths (MW PEG ~ 300 Da) self-assembles into larger-sized particles and exhibit superior bioactivity. These formulations, when applied to our in vivo tumor model, were able to better slow tumor growth compared to our free drug control. Collectively, our results highlighted design rules for application of a cationic graft copolymer structure for drug delivery, and adding understanding of another tool in the drug delivery arsenal.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Fiber Density Promotes Tip Cell Formation to Initiate Angiogenesis
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Angiogenesis is the process of extending microvasculature from pre-existing blood vessels and plays a critical role in development, tissue homeostasis, and disease progression. This process is initiated when normally quiescent endothelial cells lining the walls of blood vessels transition into activated tip cells that can degrade and invade the surrounding extracellular matrix (ECM). Invading tip cells then lead trailing stalk cells to collectively migrate, eventually resulting in the formation of patent neovessels. While many pro-angiogenic soluble factors have been identified, how physical properties of the ECM influence tip cell formation remains less explored. Here, we engineered a microfluidic 3D tip cell formation assay composed of a lumenized endothelialized arteriole-scale channel fully embedded in a user-defined ECM. To examine the influence of matrix fibers on mediating tip cell formation, we integrated fiber-reinforced fibrin hydrogels with this assay. Briefly, linear high-molecular-weight dextran (86 kDa) was functionalized with vinyl sulfone (a UV-initiated photocrosslinkable group) and dissolved at 0.6 g ml -1 in Milli-Q water and dimethylformamide with 0.015% Irgacure 2959 photoinitiator. This polymer solution was electrospun into fiber mats and selectively photocrosslinked and processed into fiber segments with tunable diameter, length, and stiffness that were functionalized for cell adhesion with the peptide CGRGDS. Embedding fiber segments within fibrin hydrogels enabled tunability of fiber density independent of fibrin weight % (allowing us to maintain a constant bulk hydrogel density, stiffness, and pore size). We found that increasing the density of fibers enhanced tip cell formation and invasion into fibrin hydrogels. Supportive of an endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, tip cells in our assay exhibited traits associated with mesenchymal cells including migratory capacity, the ability to degrade the surrounding matrix, development of actomyosin-protrusions, and loss of vascular endothelial cadherin. Taken together, this work investigates how fiber density, an important physical attribute of the ECM, regulates tip cell formation and suggests that a fibrous topography promotes the transition of quiescent endothelial cells towards a mesenchymal phenotype. A greater understanding of the mechanobiology underlying tip cell formation and function is critical to our understanding of angiogenesis and in the future could aid in the development of pro-angiogenic therapies and implantable biomaterials.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Exploring a Missing Mechanism That Links Redox Signaling to the Actin Cytoskeleton
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: In the cell, reactive oxygen species (ROS) and the actin cytoskeleton work together to control a large range of activities, such as immune response, neural growth, formation of blood vessels, and spreading of cancer cells. However, our understanding of how ROS crosstalks to actin is very limited which has hindered the development of intervening agents. My project is to determine the biochemical mechanism by which a major generator of ROS molecules named NOX and a central regulator of the actin cytoskeleton named WAVE interact with each other. This interaction may serve as a key linkage between ROS and actin in the cell. To understand this mechanism, we use recombinant protein production and various biochemical assays to determine if and how a protein named p47phox can serve as a bridge to bring NOX and WAVE together. We design various mutant proteins to map the regions responsible for p47phox binding to NOX and WAVE, respectively. We also test if p47phox binding to the WAVE Regulatory Complex (WRC) to promote formation of the actin cytoskeleton. This knowledge will help in the understanding of how the cell coordinates ROS signaling and the actin cytoskeleton to drive various processes and has the potential to reveal new targets for therapeutic development.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Scaling Down DNA-Based Information Storage
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: DNA offers extremely dense and long-term information storage capabilities, enabling the ability to accommodate growing data storage needs as a potentially transformative archival medium. Recent advancements in DNA synthesis and sequencing have created the potential for storage systems of useful sizes 1,2 . Here, we focus on miniaturizing the storage of DNA files through the development of a microfluidic device capable of selective file separations 3,4 . Our design creates polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) microfluidic reaction chambers to extract specific files using chemical handles and modified magnetic beads. We optimize the system for bead mobility across an incorporated air gap that allows for an effective physical separation of the desired file. To visually demonstrate strand retrieval, we capture 20 nucleotide (nt) fluorescently labeled primers and track them using fluorescence microscopy. We then expand to double stranded DNAs with variable lengths and show successful and specific file recovery by fragment analyzer and qPCR analyses. After file separation, we determined that the remaining solution is unaltered and can be recycled to the storage library for future use. This system provides potential physical designs for automatable and reusable DNA storage devices. References Takahashi, N. C., et al. Demonstration of End-to-End Automation of DNA Data Storage. https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Modulation of Adjuvant Loading and Degradation Profiles of Biocompatible Polymeric Nanoparticles for Immune Stimulation
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) hydrogels are commonly used in reparative tissue engineering and regenerative medicine due to their biocompatibility, hydrophilicity, and slow rate of degradation. Similarly, these desirable properties make PEG diacrylate (PEGDA) nanoparticles (NP) an attractive platform for delivery of therapeutic vaccines. Binding immunostimulatory ligands (adjuvants) to delivery platforms with a slow rate of degradation would encourage long-acting immune stimulation and thereby increase efficacy of vaccines. Therefore, our objective is to characterize the effect of modulus of PEGDA NP on rate of degradation and of NP surface density of CpG ODN for enhanced, sustained immunostimulatory effect. Aminated NPs for ligand attachment were synthesized by first mixing a pre-particle solution, which was emulsified in silicone oil and exposed to UV light to initiate polymerization. Pre-particle solution contained 50% or 30% wt/wt total solids in methanol consisting of 88% crosslinker [PEG diacrylate (PEGDA, Mn=700)], 10% cationic functional monomer [2-aminoethyl methacrylate], 1% photoinitiator [diphenyl(2,4,6-trimethylbenzoyl)phosphine oxide (TPO)], and 1% dye [Rhodamine B]. Particle degradation was monitored over 4 weeks using thermogravitational analysis (TGA), dynamic light scattering (DLS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and Rhodamine B release in pH 5, 7.4, and 10 buffers via fluorescence. A bifunctional linker, SMCC (succinimidyl 4-(N-maleimidomethyl) cyclohexane-1-carboxylate) was conjugated to NP free amines and the 5’ modified thiol on CpG. CpG loading was confirmed by UV-Vis spectrophotometry at 260 nm to measure amount of unbound nucleic acid concentration in the supernatant. TGA showed linear decrease in particle mass in both 50% and 30% total solids PEGDA NP formulations of all pH buffers over 4 weeks, suggesting bulk erosion of the polymer matrix of the NP. RITC release in solution increased sharply over week 1 of buffer storage, then was maintained from weeks 1-4. While this is indicative of bulk erosion, previous studies note the high hydrophilicity and small size of RITC could result in diffusive leaching into solution rather than matrix degradation. DLS measurements of hydrodynamic diameter and zeta potential were measured to be 273 ± 4 nm and 23.9 ± 4.9, respectively. The net positive charge of unfunctionalized PEGDA-NP suggest presence of free amines on the NP surface and PEGDA NP were functionalized with CpG ODN of varied surface densities. Overall, this work demonstrated that PEGDA NP exhibit slow degradation profiles similar to those expected for PEG hydrogels. PEGDA NP therefore remain an attractive candidate for long-acting immune stimulation.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: CRISPR Screen to Investigate Contributors to Paracellular Barrier Formation in Vitro
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Barrier-forming cells fulfil an important role in the body by regulating paracellular transport and ultimately protecting homeostasis. To elucidate potential participants in paracellular barrier formation, we performed an arrayed CRISPR knockout screen across 8400 human genes. For the screen, we used Caco2 cells, an immortalized barrier-forming gut epithelial cell line. Our Caco2 cells constitutively express Cas-9 and are robust enough to tolerate high-throughput screening conditions. The Caco2 cells were seeded at a defined density in transfection medium into 96-well plates containing the arrayed gRNA. The cells underwent reverse transfection for 24-hours before Anti-Anti was added to the media to protect against contamination. The cells were maintained in culture for four days before we induced the barrier by switching to Neurobasal media. After six days in Neurobasal media, the cells were fixed and stained for ZO-1, a tight-junction protein that localizes to the paracellular membrane in barrier-forming cells. Each well was then imaged in a Z-stack in four locations with the ImageXpress Micro XL. The screen was performed in two replicates across 109 plates. Images from both replicates were analyzed with MATLAB code to quantify variation in barrier continuity and tortuosity. Positive hits from the screen will be confirmed and tested for barrier permeability in our human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) model and a Zebrafish model.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Bioreactor Design for the Maturation and Organization of Engineered Cardiac Patches
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Introduction: About 40,000 babies are born with a congenital heart defect (CHD) every year in the United States. Approximately 25% of these babies require surgery within their first year. The current materials available to surgeons for the reconstruction of CHDs are exclusively acellular and inert, limiting the size and location of patched repair and often lead to arrhythmias. Living engineered cardiac patches (ECPs) that integrate with the heart could reduce arrhythmias and allow for more extensive repairs. In vivo native cardiac tissue consists of highly organized layers and structures. We hypothesize that directional and physiological application of strain, sheer stress, and electrical stimulation can direct ECP maturation, organization, and trabeculation. In this study, we designed a bioreactor capable of presenting directional shear strain and electrical stimulation to ECPs grown in vitro . Methods: A bioreactor was designed using Solidworks to fit three ECPs that measure 8 mm in diameter and 2 mm in height and two carbon electrodes. A fluid mechanics computational model was run in COMSOL Multiphysics in order to determine physiologically relevant flow and pressure profiles. The bioreactor was then 3D-printed using Formlabs’ Dental SG Resin , which is an autoclavable, nontoxic, not biodegradable, nonporous, and UV-transparent material. The final design of the 3D-printed reaction chamber is compatible with the adapters, fittings, and tubing necessary for the full model. Results: The fluid mechanics simulation of the final model showed that the bioreactor supports the targeted physiologically relevant shear stress of 10 dyne/cm 2 . Throughout system operation, laminar flow is maintained as fluid flows across the chamber and perfuses through the ECPs. When in contact with the ECPs, carbon electrodes attached to an electrical source will electrically stimulate the cardiomyocytes to contract simultaneously. The bioreactor was printed using an autoclavable, nontoxic, and non-biodegradable dental resin capable of adjustable pressures, flow profiles, and electrical pacing. Discussion and Conclusion: This study presents a bioreactor chamber that can be 3D-printed out of Dental SG Resin and is shown in computational flow models to maintain physiologic pressures, shear flow, and electrical stimulation through an ECP. Future experiments include flow testing through the device and evaluation of cell viability, proliferation, organization, tissue morphology, vascularization, contractile force, and synchronization. The bioreactor will later be incorporated into a control system that provides automated ECP differentiation and maturation using encapsulated pluripotent stem cells.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Engineering Escherichia coli for Methanol-Dependent Growth and Production
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: An abundance of methane from natural gas reserves has raised interest in engineering synthetic methylotrophs that can utilize methane or methanol, the oxidized form of methane, for growth and chemical production. Synthetic methylotrophs are non-methylotrophic platform organisms that have been engineered to utilize reduced C1 compounds. Since native methylotrophs lack many of the well-developed genetic engineering tools that platform organisms possess, the development of robust synthetic methylotrophs is of considerable interest. Our lab previously developed a synthetic Escherichia coli methylotroph that consumes 1 mol of methanol with 1 mol of glucose concurrently, making this strain “methanol-dependent.” This allows the sugar feedstock cost to be reduced by supplying a portion of the carbon substrate as methanol, which is less expensive. Using adaptive laboratory evolution and process optimization, we report improvements to growth and acetone production. One such evolved strain exhibited robust methanol-dependent growth in glucose minimal medium, whereas negligible growth was observed using the ancestral strain. To improve acetone production (from acetyl-CoA via enzymes from Clostridium ), yeast extract was supplemented to this minimal medium to provide amino acids for biomass synthesis, allowing methanol and glucose to be used primarily for acetone production. As expected, our data demonstrate that acetone production increases with increasing yeast extract concentration (from 2 to 6 g/L). Future work will involve scale-up to a recently developed cell-recycle bioreactor system for high-titer acetone production at bench-scale. This work expands the knowledge of the synthetic methylotrophy field by highlighting the importance of using reduced C1 compounds, alone or together with sugar-based feedstocks, for the production of liquid fuels and chemicals.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Utilizing Endotracheal Tubes to Modulate Particle Deposition Profiles in a 3D-Printed Lung Model
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Design of therapeutics for aerosol delivery relies heavily on the use of deposition profiles of healthy, male patients to predict drug performance and efficiency. Delivery of aerosolized therapeutic using a device such as a nebulizer may be needed while a patient is intubated; however, it is unknown whether the presence of an endotracheal (ET) tube alters the deposition profile of a drug in the lungs. Our objective is to investigate the differences in airflow through the lungs in the presence of an ET tube and determine whether these effects can be tuned through altering parameters such as tube diameter, cuff inflation, and release outlet location to inform the formulation and administration of aerosolized therapeutics. By leveraging our 3D-printing capabilities, we can quantify particle deposition for each of the five lung lobes in an anatomically accurate model derived from patient computed tomography (CT) scans printed using the Carbon M1 3D-Printer. ET tubes with inner diameters (ID) of 7, 8 or 9 mm were compared to a clinical flow profile of a healthy male without an ET tube. Additionally, ET tube depth and cuff shape were altered to skew deposition toward one side of the lung. We found that, while altering depth had little effect on the deposition profile, altering ET tube ID did have a significant impact with the 9 mm ET tube skewing 74% (p = 0.001) of the fluorescent polystyrene 1 μm diameter particles delivered towards the right lung. A similar effect was achieved by altering the inflation of the cuff to direct 70% (p = 0.03) of the delivered particles to the right lung. These effects were also investigated at various flow rates to provide information on the optimal point of release in the breath cycle. Overall, the ID and orientation of an ET tube can have a significant effect on the efficiency of the delivery of aerosolized therapeutics to a specific region of the lung and should be considered when designing pharmaceutics and dosing for intubated patients.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Investigating Factors Affecting Oxygen Reduction Reaction on Boron Doped Diamond Electrode and Its Possible Effects on Neural Stimulation
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in neural stimulation electrochemically generates reactive oxygen species, which if diffused away into the implanted tissue, might cause tissue damage. Therefore the ORR should be as minimized in neural stimulation (JT.Morton, 1994; S.F Morgan, 2010; EM Hudak, 2017). Boron-doped diamond electrodes have attracted considerable interest as a bio-interfacing electrode material, because of their biocompatibility, wide water window, and electrochemical stability; they also have been reported to have slow kinetics for the ORR. However, few investigations have focused on how its sp 2 carbon content, or non-diamond content, can contribute to oxygen reduction. Moreover, ultranano-crystaline diamond (sp 2 abundant) was recently reported in neural interface applications, justifying the need for further understanding the effect of sp 2 carbon. In this work, we investigate how sp 2 coverage affects the ORR on polycrystalline diamond film electrodes, and also how other factors such as anodic oxidation increase ORR activity. Electrochemical redox activity of Fe 2+/3+ and Raman spectroscopy were used to characterize sp 2 content, and X-ray Photo electron spectroscopy to probe surface oxygen functional groups, before and after anodic oxidation. The electrode’s cathodic charge storage capacity (cCSC), as a measure of the relative contribution of oxygen electrochemistry in charge injection, was compared with cyclic voltammetry (200mV/s scan rate) in N2 and O2 saturated phosphate buffered saline (PBS). Preliminary results showed that diamond electrodes containing surface sp 2 carbon showed more activity towards oxygen reduction than those containing less sp 2 carbon. In addition, we found that if sp 2 containing electrode was anodically oxidized by potential scanning in dilute H 2 SO 4 , the cathodic current (presumably oxygen reduction current) increased. The increase in ORR activity after anodic oxidation could be explained by surface chemistry change or increased surface roughness (thus effective surface area). Since anodic polarization can oxidize an as-grown, primarily hydrogen-terminated diamond surface, and reaching anodic potentials during neural stimulation is inevitable, the effect of anodic oxidation should also be considered when evaluating the effect of sp 2 carbon. In the future, possible products of ORR will be investigated, and the ORR process investigated using faster scan rates to match the time scale of neural stimulation methods.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Role of Tissue Geometry in Regulating Liver Bud Morphogenesis
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Fetal liver development is a multicellular morphogenetic process that transforms an initial hepatic bud into liver tissue. A pivotal point during development occurs when the hepatic bud forms and migrates into the surrounding mesenchyme to begin rapid spatiotemporal liver growth. This particular transient stage of liver development is due to many local biomechanical signaling mechanisms that regulate hepatic architecture and migration. However, complete knowledge of this phenomenon is still insufficient. Through the application of bioengineering principles, current research looks to examine how micro-environmental matrix stiffness stimulates hepatic bud formation and migration into the mesenchyme. Our approach utilizes an in vitro model of the fetal liver bud via 3D spheroidal and toroidal culture of a model hepatic cell line (HepG2) to determine how liver bud geometry influences subsequent cell proliferation. HepG2 cells are seeded into round bottom ULA (ultra-low attachment) plates and microtissue 3D ™ devices to form compact spheroids and toroid tissues (72 hours) respectively. These tissues after harvesting are embedded into varying concentrations of Matrigel (growth factor positive) as a model of the local hepatic mesenchyme to determine an association between matrix stiffness and cellular migration. Preliminary data suggests a strong correlation between tissue geometry and migration of cells in varying concentrations of matrix. This project proposes new insights into the biomechanical mechanisms that promote liver development.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: An Electrochemical Biosensor for in-Situ Detection of Lipids By Immobilization of Cholesterol Oxidase
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Atherosclerosis is the blockage of blood flow through arteries due to plaque buildup from high cholesterol. High cholesterol does not display symptoms and can only be detected through a blood test. There is a clinical need for a device able to analyze cholesterol concentration in-situ. For the development of a biosensor for cholesterol detection, an amperometric, three-electrode system was utilized. Cholesterol oxidase (ChOx) was immobilized at the working electrode through a self-assembled monolayer (SAM) of octadecanethiol (ODT) or thioglycolic acid (TGA) and electropolymerization of pyrrole. Multiple immobilization methods were assessed through amperometric measurements and cyclic voltammetry. The cyclic voltammetry experiments were run for assessing the formation of the self-assembled monolayer, by determining a change in current measured by the sensor. The amperometric measurements were conducted for cholesterol detection along with the characterization of sensitivity of the functionalized biosensor. This study looked at different enzyme immobilization methods for creating a device that can analyze cholesterol blood composition. The obtained results show that two functionalization methods yielded different results, with a fairly good liner response curve between the sensor’s current signal and cholesterol concentration for the sensor with the pyrrole method. Future work includes further optimization of the functionalization process and tuning of the sensitivity, among others.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Optimizing Production of EV71 Virus-like-Particle from CHO Cells
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: EV71 virus-like-particle (VLP) mimics the enterovirus causing hand-foot-and-mouth disease (HFMD), an illness that is prevalent in east and southeast Asia and currently has no specific prevention method or treatment. The EV71 VLP has been shown to elicit the immune response necessary for a promising vaccine. To test the VLP’s feasibility as a vaccine candidate for HFMD, large quantities of it must be isolated. Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells transfected with the EV71 VLP vector used are a unique system in that the cells are capable of continuously producing EV71 VLP without inducing cell lysis, a common problem in cells transfected with other variations of the VLP vector. To optimize EV71 VLP production further, we conditioned expressing CHO cells with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) or sodium butyrate (NaB) and observed differences in EV71 VLP amounts qualitatively via western blot imaging. Additionally, we performed microtiter BCA assays for total protein quantification to see if this method could be used to quantify the differences in VLP production. The optimal percentage of DMSO for small volume plate cultures (3ml of media) was found to be 2.0%, and the optimal concentration of NaB for 3ml and 10ml plate cultures was found to be 1.0mM. We concluded the BCA assay is an inappropriate method for quantifying VLP production due to its inherent relativity and lack of specificity for the VLP. In the future, obtaining EV71 VLP may be further improved by conditioning simultaneously with DMSO and NaB, by developing a cost-effective method for specifically quantifying EV71 VLP, by scaling up production with CHO cells to larger volumes or suspended culture, and by optimizing purification of the VLP via ion exchange chromatography.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Development of Mycobacterium Smegmatis As a Host Strain for Polyketide Synthase Production
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Polyketide synthases (PKSs) are enzymes that synthesize a biologically important family of complex chemicals called polyketides, which include antibiotics, anticancer, and immunosuppressant drugs. Due to their highly complex architectures, polyketides are difficult to synthesize via traditional organic chemistry means. Through bioengineering, scientists are able to genetically modify PKSs to selectively produce polyketides of interest such as adipic acid, methyl ketones, and chiral building blocks. However, commonly used heterologous hosts for PKS production, such as Escherichia coli and Streptomyces, often produce misfolded, truncated, and non-functional PKSs or they can be challenging to genetically manipulate and grow slowly. In response to this need, we seek to develop Mycobacterium smegmatis as a new PKS host due to its more easily manipulated genome, availability of genetic tools, relatively fast growth rate, and ability to naturally produce precursors for biosynthesis. To assay for phosphopantetheinylation, an essential post-translational modification of PKSs made by phosphopantetheinyl transferase (PPTase), we introduced the gene bpsA , which encodes a blue-pigment indigoidine synthetase, into wild type M. smegmatis . We found that wild type M. smegmatis produced indigoidine, which indicates the presence of an active PPTase. Furthermore, we genomically integrated a second copy of a PPTase under the control of a constitutive promoter to improve the ability of the host to phosphopanteheinylate heterologous PKSs and integrated T7 RNA polymerase to make the host compatible with IPTG inducible T7 promoter expression systems. Additionally, we developed an IPTG inducible T7 promoter expression plasmid, containing a his-tagged RFP under an inducible T7 promoter for protein purification. Flow cytometry was used to study the inducibility of the system by measuring fluorescence levels of induced and non-induced M. smegmatis containing the T7 expression plasmid, further providing evidence that these genetic tools will be a useful platform for purifying PKSs or for fermentative production of polyketides.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Critical Flux during Tangential Flow Microfiltration of Precipitated Proteins
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: There is considerable clinical interest in both polyclonal Immunoglobulin G (IgG) and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) as biotherapuetics. Polyclonal IgG is currently purified from blood serum using an ethanol-based precipitation, while the initial step in the purification of most mAbs is by bind-and-elute Protein A affinity chromatography. We have been exploring the use of ZnCl 2 – PEG combinations for continuous precipitation of IgG / mAbs, exploiting the high product titer of current mAb products (>5 g/L). Long term operation of the system can be achieved by operating the membrane unit at a filtrate flux below the critical flux for the onset of fouling. The objective of this particular project was to explore opportunities for increasing the critical flux, including the use of co-flow to provide a more constant transmembrane pressure drop throughout the module. The precipitation of IgG was conducted in a tubular precipitation reactor with sequential inline addition of ZnCl 2 (a crosslinking agent) and PEG (a volume exclusion agent). High IgG yield (>99%) was obtained in the precipitate. The precipitated IgG was then concentrated and washed using hollow fiber polyethersulfone membranes. The critical flux was evaluated using a flux-stepping procedure, with the transmembrane pressure evaluated as a function of time during each constant flux interval. The addition of co-flow did not cause any measurable increase in the critical flux. However, the critical flux could be increased by using membranes with higher permeability. The critical flux was also a function of the aging of the precipitates, with fresh precipitates found to have a larger mean particle size. These results provide important insights into the development of effective tangential flow microfiltration systems for use in continuous protein purification by precipitation.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Rewiring Amino Acid Biosynthesis Via Regulator Modulation and Operon Overexpression Improves Methanol Utilization in a Synthetic Escherichia coli Methylotroph
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The abundance of natural gas has made reduced one carbon compounds like methane and methanol attractive feedstocks for commodity chemical and fuel production, particularly in bioprocesses where they can replace more expensive sugar substrates. While many organisms natively consume one carbon substrates, these microbes (known as methylotrophs) lack many of the well-developed genetic engineering tools that platform organisms possess, which limits their production capacity. Engineering methylotrophy in industrially popular organisms is a promising alternative – in particular, progress has been made to engineer Escherichia coli to consume methanol. However, to date, no E. coli strain has been developed that can grow on methanol as a sole carbon substrate. We have identified amino acid biosynthesis as a crucial bottleneck to sole methylotrophy using 13 C labelling – while most metabolites in glycolysis and the TCA cycle show substantial methanol incorporation, labelling in amino acids is significantly lower, and many amino acids lack methanol carbon entirely. Starting with an E. coli ΔfrmA variant expressing heterologous ribulose monophosphate (RuMP) pathway enzymes, we achieved greater methanol incorporation into amino acids using a variety of metabolic engineering strategies. Improvements were made by modulating regulators of amino acid biosynthesis, overexpressing enzymes for the biosynthesis of specific amino acids, and utilizing enzyme variants that do not possess traditional allosteric inhibition. The best variants from each method were then combined, yielding additive benefits to methanol incorporation. The resulting strains represent unique starting points for achieving sole methylotrophy via adaptive evolution or further metabolic engineering.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Grape Ripening inside and Outside the Fruit Region
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Grape growth and wine production are dependent on location, temperature, and time. The time required for grapes to ripen also varies by species of grape and location of the grape cluster on the vine. There are two main regions on a grape vine, the fruit region (FR), and outside the fruit region (OFR). The FR is the lower-middle area of the vine where the majority of the fruit grows. The region OFR consists of the upper part of the vine where there is less fruit and more foliage. Throughout many harvest periods, Fero Vineyards & Winery has determined that grapes in the OFR ripen at a slower rate than the fruit in the FR. This is due to the amount of direct sunlight and leaf exposure. FR grapes receive a moderate to high amount of direct sunlight because the leaves are pruned in this area and are not covering the fruit. The OFR grapes receive less direct sunlight because they are covered by leaves. Direct sunlight has photosynthetic effects on ripening rates of grapes through its effects on the vine’s leaves. This is because leaves provide the grapes with sugar to make them sweeter. Thus grapes outside of the fruit region do not receive the benefits of sunlight which affects their rate of ripening. Wine production proceeds almost exclusively from FR grapes, presenting an opportunity to reduce waste and increase production by determining when OFR grapes can be harvested. While general characteristics of wine grape behavior is well known, regional variations in climate and sunlight require any model of grape ripening to be based primarily on local data. This research project focuses on the time dependence of ripeness for Pinot Noir, Lemberger, Riesling, and Gruner Veltliner grapes both FR and OFR. Ripeness is determined by the balance of brix (sugar content), ph, and titratable acidity. This data will aid Fero Vineyards & Winery in harvest time estimates and possible economic benefits from creating new OFR-based products. Sources: Zoecklein, B W, and B H Gump. Evaluation of Grape Maturity and the Factors Impacting Maturity . www.apps.fst.vt.edu/extension/enology/downloads/wm_issues/Fruit%20Maturity/Evaluation%20of%20Grape%20Maturity%20and%20the%20Factors%20Impacting%20Maturity.pdf .

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Sustained Delivery of Phenotypic Regulators of T-Cells
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: T-cells are the critical helper, effector and regulatory cells of the adaptive immunity and are essential for life. However, defects in their number and function can contribute to tissue and organ specific inflammatory autoimmune diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis, etc.). A shared feature of T-cell mediated autoimmune disorders is an upregulation of pro-inflammatory T-cell subsets, often accompanied by a deficiency in the number of regulatory T-cells (T regs ). T regs lose their capacity to modulate the function of other immune cells and adopt a pro-inflammatory phenotype, secreting pro-inflammatory cytokines. This process is mediated, in part, through the IL-6/IL-6R axis in a pro-inflammatory microenvironment. We hypothesize that the local metabolic regulation of T-cells in affected tissues can restore their numbers and function, thereby mitigating the symptoms and underlying cause of inflammation. To test the hypothesis, we use small molecule immunomodulators (SMIs) of T-cells that have been previously shown to modulate T-cell phenotype in vitro. However, their small size and hydrophobicity precludes efficient delivery and therefore require high doses which contributes to undesired systemic side effects in vivo. To enhance the efficacy of SMIs, we designed a biomaterial-based system to sustain the local delivery of SMIs and suppress autoreactive T-cells and improve T reg function. We developed a polymer hydrogel to retain and release the bioactive SMIs by directly conjugating the SMIs to a biopolymer via an ester linkage in a crosslinked hydrogel. We used spectrophotometry to quantify SMI loading onto the scaffold and cell counting and flow cytometry to determine any expansion and phenotypic changes. We characterized the conjugate using spectrophotometry (λ = 360 nm) and quantified a ~5% degree of substitution of SMI. Furthermore, the SMI-polymer conjugate reduced IL-17 + T-cells by ~15% and expanded IL-10 + T-cells by ~2 fold compared to the controls without any SMI stimulation. The reduction in IL-17 + T-cells was directly proportional to the reduction in IL-6 receptor expression on T-cells. In summary, the SMI-polymer conjugate modulated the activity of autoreactive T-cells and improved T reg function, supporting its utility as a phenotypic regulator of T-cells.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Rheological Study of Natural Starch Biomaterial for Building Biomimetic Immune Tissue
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Mimicking lymph tissue is challenging, yet crucial for understanding cell-mediated immune responses, and translating into clinical immunotherapy treatments. This study introduces a new class of 3D bioink which could advance 3D tissue engineering and facilitate fast growing of immunotherapy treatment strategy.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Modeling the Controlled Release of Risperidone from PLGA Microsphere Formulations
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: My research is focused on how to improve the predictions of the in vivo effects of controlled release of the specific drug, risperidone. Risperidone is used to treat schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and autistic irritability. To accomplish our goal, we are using an existing mathematical model that simulates how a general drug leaves a poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) polymer (PLGA) microsphere in vitro. We are adapting the model considering the characteristics of risperidone. So far, we have taken existing in vitro data from literature and digitized it. From there we considered the first phase of in vitro release after an initial burst to be a diffusion-controlled release regime described by Fickian diffusion with a constant diffusion coefficient. We used parameter estimation to fit the Risperidone initial burst amount and diffusion coefficients through different formulations of microspheres. Now we are looking into what happens, particularly to the second release regime of pore degradation-controlled release, when certain properties are changed, such as particle size, molecular weight, and the PLA/PGA ratios. Later we will adapt the in vitro model to an in vivo one using mass transport and pharmacokinetics of risperidone released from PLGA to create a prediction for how risperidone is delivered in the body. We will validate the final in vivo model with existing data. This approach can be compared with proposed in vitro-in vivo correlations in the literature.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Extraction of Dicarboxylic Acids from Fermentation Broth and Analysis By HPLC
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Long dicarboxylic acids (DCAs), are used in the production of polymers, polyesters, and personal care products. However, the chemical process to make these compounds is unfavorable due the petroleum-based feedstock necessary to start the reactions. One alternative, renewable, and efficient method for the production of DCAs is through biotechnology. This study focused on improving methods for extraction and analysis of C18 DCAs in fermentation broth. We tested alternative methods of optimizing extraction conditions in order to reduce costs because pure C18:0 and C18:1 DCAs can sell for approximately 122 $/g. Solubility tests were performed on C18 DCA, C12 DCA, and stearic acid and it was determined that C12 DCA may be an adequate substitute for C18 DCA in testing; however using C12 DCA required changes to the analytical method in order to resolve peaks. The optimized method for analyzing C12 DCA used a decreased flow rate and an increased column oven temperature. The mobile phase was changed from an isocratic mixture of methanol, water, and acetic acid (v/v, 90:9.9:0.1) to a gradient between water with 0.1% (v/v) formic acid and acetonitrile with 0.1% (v/v) formic acid. Finally, an extraction method was developed for C12 DCA that had an average recovery yield of 92.9%. By optimizing the extraction process with C12 DCA, we obtained useful information for the process of optimizing extraction of C18 from fermentation broth.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Critical Role of Lipin-2 in the Development of Chronic Multifocal Osteomyelitis
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Chronic Recurrent Multifocal Osteomyelitis (CRMO) is an autoinflammatory bone disorder that causes patients to exhibit chronically active or recurrent sterile bone lesions at multiple sites. The chronic multifocal osteomyelitis (cmo) mouse carries a mutation in the Pstpip2 gene and develops IL-1b mediated sterile bone disorder reminiscent of human CRMO. On the other hand, mutation in the LPIN2 gene that encodes for , a vital molecule in lipid metabolism, is known to cause an autoinflammatory disease called Majeed syndrome which is characterized by CRMO, dyserythropoietic anemia, and may have neutrophilic skin inflammation. Previous reports have shown that cholesterol levels in the cells regulate IL1b production by the Lpin2 deficient immune cells. To investigate the cholesterol synthesis in the bone marrow cells from cmo and Lpin2 deficient mice, expression of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis was performed using quantitative PCR method. We found that the expression of several cholesterol biosynthesis pathway genes is attenuated in cmo mice-derived cells, suggesting that difference in the levels of cholesterol in the cells might be involved in the susceptibility/resistance from the cmo disease.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: A Systems Biology Model of Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells and Cancer Immunotherapy
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Some malignant diseases can cause major changes to the immune system, which prevents the body from properly protecting itself from threats. Immuno-suppressive diseases like cancer, HIV, and AIDS disable the body’s ability to fight against pathogens. This begs the question that there must be a procedure to restore the body’s immune system, so it can function properly. This is why myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are extremely valuable to the immune system. These cells can serve many functions because they change into different types of cells depending on the situation at hand. When the immune system is activated, an MDSC can change into macrophages or dendritic cells, but when the immune system is not activated, it stays as a MDSC. Macrophages and dendritic cells are white blood cells that can sense a pathogen in the body, alert the immune system, and destroy it. Tumor Associated Macrophages or TAMs are the type of macrophages MDSCs morph into when they do differentiate. TAMs have been shown to have the potential of interacting negatively with the tumor cells by attacking it. The methodology of this research will use mathematical modeling of differential equations using MATLAB software to model the dynamics of MDSC and TAMs and their interactions with tumors. Mathematical modeling gives the flexibility of testing many different stimuli easily (quickly and cheaply) and mechanistically. I have combined two existing models and data from the literature. The first model considers MDSCs in the tumor microenvironment without any treatment and with a treatment. This model tests how each change affects the MDSC response. The second model shows how TAMs can be activated into two phenotypes to attack or ignore tumors. Validation of the combined MATLAB model will be done by comparing to data from collaborators and from published experimental studies.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Modeling the Dissolution of Prednisolone Loaded Polyvinyl Alcohol Films
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Prednisolone loaded polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) films were prepared and characterized to find density and glass transition temperature. Drug release and mass loss studies of these films were conducted in order to establish a predictive and tunable model that could be used in order to formulate pills specific to meet unique release requirements. The studies were conducted at different solution volumes (10 mL and 50 mL) at pH 6.8, as well as with and without the surfactant Tween 80 (thought to imitate conditions in the intestines) in order to create a comprehensive drug release system. The addition of Tween 80 allowed for the complete dissolution of the drug in supernatant within 2 hours, while other changes in the surroundings, such as change in volume, and changes to the film, such as film thickness and drug loading, did not largely influence the release kinetics. The experimental results (concentration profile with time) were fitted using the Noyes-Whitney Approximation, a surface erosion drug dissolution model based on Fick’s first law, which produces a good correlation (R 2 > 0.9) with simultaneous prediction of physical parameters, solubility and lumped rate constant. The developed model and experimental procedures for the release of prednisolone from the PVA films will be significant for future film based drug delivery development and design.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Effect of Feed Flow Rate and Precipitate Concentration on the Precipitation Process for the Purification of Monoclonal Antibody
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Precipitation can be a highly effective step in the initial capture of monoclonal antibodies (mAb). High yield of the precipitates can be produced continuously in a tubular reactor with cross-linking and volume exclusion agents. The integration with tangential flow microfiltration for the dewatering and wash stages would allow for high removal of impurities creating a feasible fully continuous precipitation process for the purification of mAbs. However, current issues with this process are the low impurity removal rates and low yield of the final product. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effect of feed flow rate and the precipitate concentration on increasing the critical flux and product yield. The higher the critical flux, the higher the permeate flux, which would enable the membranes to remove more impurities. In our experiments, human serum Immunoglobulin G (IgG) was used as a model protein. The IgG precipitates (99.8% yield) were produced through a tubular reactor using zinc chloride and polyethylene glycol as the cross-linking and volume exclusion agent, respectively. The solutions were mixed with static mixers with a residence time of 30 seconds. Critical flux experiments were performed with a total recycle system, with the inlet feed flow rate varied to examine its effect on the critical flux. Re-dissolution experiments were performed using different IgG precipitate concentrations and buffer conditions to improve the overall product yield. Results have shown that a decrease in feed flow rate can increase the critical flux, and forming precipitates using a higher protein titer can prevent product re-dissolution and increase yield. These results provide important insights for the improved design of a precipitation – microfiltration process for initial capture/purification of a monoclonal antibody product.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: AKT but Not MYC Promotes Reactive Oxygen Species-Mediated Cell Death in Oxidative Culture
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Oncogenes can generate metabolic vulnerabilities in cancer cells. Here, we tested how AKT and MYC affect the ability of cells to shift between respiration and glycolysis. Using immortalized mammary epithelial cells, we discovered that constitutively active AKT but not MYC induced cell death in galactose culture, where cells must rely on oxidative phosphorylation for energy generation. However, the negative effects of AKT were short-lived, and AKT-expressing cells recommenced growth after ~15 days in galactose. To identify the mechanisms regulating AKT-mediated cell death, we used metabolomics and found that AKT cells dying in galactose upregulated glutathione metabolism. Next, using proteomics, we discovered that AKT-expressing cells dying in galactose upregulated nonsense-mediated mRNA decay, a marker of sensitivity to oxidative stress. We measured levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and discovered that galactose induced ROS in cells expressing AKT but not MYC. Additionally, ROS were required for the galactose-induced death of AKT-expressing cells. We then tested whether these findings could be replicated in breast cancer cell lines with constitutively active AKT signaling. Indeed, we found that galactose induced rapid cell death in breast cancer cell lines and that ROS were required for galactose-induced cell death. Our collective results demonstrate that AKT but not MYC induces a metabolic vulnerability in cancer cells, namely the restricted flexibility to use oxidative phosphorylation.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Design & Development of 3D Printed Polymeric Structure for Pharmaceutical(s) Delivery
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: 3D printing as an advanced manufacturing process provides a unique opportunity to design and develop complex structure as opposed to using traditional manufacturing techniques. 3D printing encompasses the benefits: agile and robust manufacturing, reduce the cost, reduction in turnaround times, and reliability. 3D printing of pharmaceuticals is especially advantageous for personalized medicine, making multi-drug pills where current manufacturing processes unable to do that. Traditional pharmaceutical processes and tools for the manufacturing of pills have changed relatively little for over a century. Traditional pharmaceutical manufacturing focus on large-scale batches and little flexibility in the manufacturing process due to the multi-step process. Current direct compression manufacturing process unable to make multi-drug pills due to challenges of multiple active material processing, limitation on compression, and pill size control. As an advanced manufacturing technique, 3D printing has the potential to develop personalized medicine, multi-drug pills. It is an exciting branch of research and it requires research and development to utilize the full potential. The research goal for this work is the design and development of a 3D printed polymeric structure for pharmaceutical(s) delivery. There are several 3D printing processes available and we will focus on pressure-assisted microsyringe (PAM) printing. PAM is well suited for the pharmaceutical industry due to its capability of handling materials at low temperature. Specific research objectives will be (i) develop a methodology for manufacturing 3D printed structure suitable for pharmaceutical(s) delivery, (ii) study the process parameters (nozzle size, printing pressure) that will affect the printed structure. The research outcome is expected to contribute to 3D printing fundamentals and develop personalized medicine.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Quantifying Mass Changes at a Peg Surface Complexed with Alpha-Cyclodextrin
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: αCyclodextrin is a unique molecule because of its hydrophobic interior cavity and hydrophilic exterior. This interior cavity can create inclusion complexes with a variety of hydrophobic guest molecules, including resveratrol, a hydrophobic molecule naturally found in red wine and grapes. This system has been well quantified using Electron Impedance Spectroscopy, Cyclic Voltammetry, and X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy, but not yet with electrochemical Quartz Crystal Microbalance (eQCM). eQCM provides insight into the surface coverage of the system. It quantifies the bonds between the Poly(ethyl-glycol) and αCyclodextrin by measuring the changes in mass, as a function of frequency change. Understanding this system has implications for the field of biosensors, point-of-care tools, and any sensor that could benefit from the sensing of a guest molecule with properties similar to Resveratrol. The use of eQCM allows for mass measurements of the αCyclodextrin-PEG system. Understanding the mass changes in such a system allows for analysis of reusability and reproducibility in the context of reusable sensors. Within a flow cell, eQCM, setup, αCyclodextrin-PEG system was modified onto a gold electrode using thiol-poly(ethyl-glycol) carboxyl-terminated (PEG-CT). A decrease in frequency (proportional to an increase in mass) would be seen upon PEG-CT attachment. After this modification, αCD was introduced to the system and attached to the PEG-CT molecules further decreasing the frequency (increasing the mass).Upon introduction of Resveratrol to the system, Resveratrol and αCD create an inclusion complex, removing the αCD from the surface, which would display a decrease in mass and increase in frequency.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Salt Loading Effects in Cathepsin B KO Mice on Renal Enac and Blood Pressure
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Cathepsin B is among a myriad of proteases that cleaves and activates the renal epithelial sodium channel (ENaC). ENaC expressed in the distal tubule and collecting duct cells of the kidney play a key role in sodium balance and blood pressure regulation. Salt loading results in the development of hypertension in the salt sensitive kidney. We investigated the mechanism by which salt loading regulates the activity of Cathepsin B and ENaC in the kidney. We hypothesized that Cathepsin B knock out mice develop hypertension after salt loading, but the effect is attenuated when compared to wild type mice. We examined ENaC subunit protein expression in kidney cortex lysates and native tissues by Western blotting and immunohistochemistry, respectively. We performed activity assays for cathepsin B and other proteases that cleave and activate ENaC including furin and kallikrein. We measured urinary sodium and potassium levels using a SmartLyte analyzer to correlate changes in blood pressure in these mice. Taken together, our data suggest cathepsin B plays an essential role in regulating ENaC activity and blood pressure, but other proteases contribute to this regulation.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Production of Dicarboxylic Acids By Biotransformation of Oleic Acid Using Candida Viswanathii
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Dicarboxylic acids (DCAs) are wildly used in biopolymer production and personal care products. Among various DCAs, long-chain dicarboxylic acids (LCDCAs) are used mostly in production of biodegradable polyesters and polyamides such as nylon. Production of DCA through biotransformation has drawn great interest from researchers recently for sustainability reasons. Previous studies have demonstrated that the yeast Candida viswanathii can potentially be used for production of dicarboxylic acids from a variety of different fatty acids, some of which are found in distillers corn oil (DCO), a byproduct of dry grind ethanol production. In this work, small scale fermentations of Candida viswanathii under various controlled conditions were conducted. As one of the major components in DCO, oleic acid was chosen as a model feedstock. Conversions with both the free acid and the methyl ester were explored. Products extracted from fermentation broth were analyzed with a previously developed high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) method. Initial results indicate the consumption rate of oleic acid was faster than that of methyl oleate. Among components extracted from fermentation broth, DCAs were detected at lower levels than expected based on feedstock consumption. Improvements to the extraction protocol are being explored to ensure high recovery of DCA. In addition, interfering medium components imposed difficulty in quantifying concentrations of DCA with the existing HPLC method. Adjustment of column temperature in the HPLC method reduced such signal interference.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Testing Methyltransferase Inhibitors to Therapeutically Target Glioblastoma Cancer Cells
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Glioblastoma is an extremely aggressive and deadly cancer where patients have limited therapeutic treatment options. Currently, most patients must resort to chemotherapy or surgery in order to treat glioblastoma. Therefore, developing a viable therapeutic treatment option for patients suffering from glioblastoma would represent a major advancement. The process of protein methylation has been an understudied cellular process despite its importance, and the Graham Lab has developed novel proteomic techniques utilizing mass spectrometry to study peptide methylation. Due to the proximity of the MTAP gene (5-methylthioadenosine phosphorylase) to the tumor suppressor CDKN2A , MTAP is deleted in about 50% of glioblastomas. When MTAP is deleted, there is a buildup in the concentration of MTA (methylthioadenosine), which acts as a natural inhibitor for PRMT5, a methyltransferase enzyme responsible for cellular protein methylation, further sensitizing the cell to drug inhibition of PRMT5. Data from the Graham Lab indicates that PRMT1 and PRMT5 inhibition have a synergistic effect. Furthermore, this trend should only selectively target glioblastoma cells that have MTAP deleted, as normal cells with MTAP should be able to withstand drug-mediated inhibition. We hypothesize that when both PRMT1 and PRMT5 are inhibited within a cancer cell deleted for MTAP , the cell will die because its methyltransferase enzymes will no longer be able to methylate essential proteins. To test this hypothesis, we will culture MTAP -deleted cancer cell lines engineered to overexpress either luciferase (negative control) or MTAP (reconstitution of MTAP). We will treat the cells with different concentrations of PRMT1 and PRMT5 drug inhibitors and analyze cell growth. We will then lyse the cells and use both High pH SCX (Strong Cation Exchange) and Sequential IAP (Immunoaffinity Purification) to enrich for methylated peptides and investigate the samples using mass spectrometry. Both SCX and IAP are powerful proteomic enrichment techniques that can be used to study methylated forms of arginine. Using the mass spectrometry results, we will identify differential methylation sites to determine the impact of global arginine methylation. We expect to pinpoint a specific concentration of PRMT1/PRMT5 inhibitors that will selectively target cells deleted for MTAP while keeping normal cells alive. We expect for the PRMT1 and PRMT5 inhibitors to display a synergistic effect. Additionally, we expect to learn more about how methyltransferase inhibitors impacts cellular survival. What we learn about protein methylation has the potential to advance our knowledge on cellular processes, and similar methods can be applied to therapeutically target different diseases.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Treatment of Low Back Pain Using an Injectable Tissue Specific Scaffold
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Low back pain (LBP) will affect 70-80% of the global population at some point during their lifetime. The main cause of LBP is known to be intervertebral disc degeneration, that causes spinal nerve impingement, leading to pain that may radiate throughout the body. Current treatment methods include prescription medications and invasive spinal fusion surgery which have many drawbacks and do not target the root of the problem. Therefore, this project involved using decellularized intervertebral disc tissue from pig as a scaffold to restore disc height and rejuvenate local cells to minimize LBP. This objective was accomplished through a thermally gelling collagen hydrogel, allowing for minimally invasive delivery to the core of the disc. Hydrogels containing decellularized tissue and greater than 2 mg/ml collagen formed macroscopically intact gels and thermal gelation kinetics results revealed that increasing collagen concentration led to a firmer and more viscous gel. Gelation time was also investigated to allow for optimal injectable delivery of the gel. Overall, intact gels were successfully synthesized by combining decellularized tissue supplemented with collagen hydrogels. Further work aims at improving the robustness of the gels.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Assessing Gut Transport of Methionine and Lysine in Fast-Growing Rainbow Trout
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Commercial aquaculture is growing at a rate of 7% per year and uses marine-derived fish meal to feed finfish and shellfish worldwide. However, fish meal supplies are limited and the future growth of aquaculture depends on the discovery of alternative sources of protein to feed fish. One promising alternative is plant-derived fish meal, however plant proteins lack sufficient levels of methionine and lysine for fish dietary requirements. A genetically selected line of rainbow trout that grows more rapidly on a plant protein diet was compared to a non-selected line. It was hypothesized that genetically selected rainbow trout uptake lysine and methionine more efficiently in their gut via more numerous amino acid transporters as compared to non-selected fish. Amino acid uptake and total amino acids were assessed in plasma over time using [C13] and [N15] isotopically labeled methionine and lysine measured by LCMS. Amino acid transporter expression in the gut was assessed using qPCR. Results show amino acid uptake in rainbow trout selected for rapid growth on a plant-protein diet is greater than the uptake observed in non-selected fish. Quantitative PCR of amino acid transporters in the proximal intestine also show various levels of expression over time consistent with levels of amino acid uptake.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Effects of Altered Quorum Sensing Regulatory Networks on Pseudomonas Aeruginosa pathogenesis
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic bacterial pathogen that commonly causes chronic lung infections in cystic fibrosis (CF) patients. People with CF acquire P. aeruginosa from their environment, after which the pathogen undergoes genetic and phenotypic changes to adapt to the lung. Many of the adaptations occur in quorum sensing (QS) systems, which regulate cell-to-cell communication that aids in coordination of group behaviors within a bacterial population. P. aeruginosa expresses a wide variety of QS-regulated phenotypes that can be used as prognostic markers of infectious stage within each patient. This study examines the link between the accumulation of QS genetic mutations and phenotypic expression in P. aeruginosa laboratory strains and clinical isolates. We utilized several plate-based and colorimetric assays to quantify the production of pyocyanin, rhamnolipids, and protease from the lab strain PA14, its QS gene deletion standards, and paired clinical early- and late-stage chronic infection isolates across 16 patients. Exoproduct production of each isolate was compared to the mean production of pooled isolates to classify high producing (QS-sufficient) and low producing (QS-deficient) isolates. We also sequenced important QS genes in these clinical isolates to identify mutations in order to link changes between genotype and phenotype. Future research of the QS regulatory networks will identify whether reversion of genotype will result in corresponding phenotypic changes in QS-deficient chronic infection isolates.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Estimation of Subcutaneous Electroosmotic Velocities in a 2-D Iontophoretic System: An Area Averaging Approach
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Although the technique is well known since approximately 3,000 BC, transdermal drug delivery became a common practice starting only five decades ago. Initially used to treat skin disorders, today’s transdermal delivery is an alternative treatment for patients with vascular limitations, epilepsy, advance pregnancy, heart condition, artificial joints, and lumps among others. Iontophoresis, a modern version of this old technique, uses electrical field gradients over the skin to more accurately and in less time deliver drug to a specific area of the body. The process facilitates the transport of species by two mechanisms, electrophoresis and electro-osmosis. Depending on the order of magnitude of the electrical field gradient one of these two mechanisms can be dominant of the procedure. Investigating the best or most effective conditions at which electro-osmosis has an improvement impact in drug delivery is the driving force for the present effort. This is the continuation and follow up of a previous contribution presented on the topic 1 . In this contribution, the mathematical governing expressions capturing the fluid dynamic of the system, coupled with the electrical field, is solved by applying the method of spatial averaging to the bulk movement of the transporting fluid. In addition, explicit analytical expressions are derived for the local and average electrostatic potential, and the local and average electroosmotic velocity. Illustrations of how a 2D electrical field can aid in increasing drug delivery with the target system. Practical conclusions and potential applications with less disruptive treatment protocol are discussed. Analysis of a 2D Iontophoretic System Using an Area Averaging Approach, AIChE Annual Meeting , Pittsburgh, PA Oct 28 - Nov 2, 2018. Alisa J. Kidwell1, Mario Oyanader2 and Steffano Oyanader.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Comparison of Mathematical Solution Approaches for a Simple Theoretical Dialysis Model
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Emerging new disciplines and technologies have made it possible to move in the direction of smaller and wearable artificial organs. This is the case of alternative treatments for renal insufficiency which may include dialysis. Miniaturization of traditional methods, such as hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, has open the doors for the development of portable and implantable devices. On the design aspect, considerable attention is been devoted to analyze the fundamental principles governing the intended down scaling for this type of applications. Typically, the analysis involves the solution of non-trivial differential equations followed by simulation of different performance scenarios. The approach, predictive in essence, makes experimental work more effective and less intense as optimal device designing can be achieved using less resources. In this contribution, the focus is on the analysis of the mathematical methods utilized to solve the fundamental differential equations describing the dialysis phenomenon. These methods may have an impact on the prediction of performance and therefore the potential design of a device. For the typical dialysis model, two mathematical methods apply to the solution of the resulting differential equations: variable separation and the asymptotic solution. In this study, the molar species continuity equation is solved analytically using these two methods and the prediction results are compared with the numerical values. A summary of these results will be provided with important insights into the development and design of wearable artificial kidneys.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Characterizing a Novel Brain-Targeted Polymeric Nanoparticle Platform
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Parkinson’s Disease (PD) is a chronic neurodegenerative disorder that leads to significant brain damage. Currently approved therapeutics treat symptoms, but do not slow down the progression of disease. There are several drugs that can slow progression, but delivery is challenging due to the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Polyanhydride nanoparticles (NPs) can improve therapeutic efficacy for brain delivery by crossing the BBB and releasing the drug at the right time. The goal of this project is to develop and characterize targeted NP-based drug delivery methods that will slow down the progression of neurodegenerative diseases, such as PD. There are multiple hurdles to delivering therapeutics to the brain. They need to cross the BBB, target the diseased area of the brain, and often deliver payloads to specific organelles or pathological features associated with cells in this area. Using a novel targeted functionalization polyanhydride NP platform, each of these hurdles can be addressed effectively and in a cascading manner. In order to optimize therapeutic efficacy, however, NP-drug interaction properties need to be well characterized. By better understanding drug-NP interactions, the NP synthesis conditions can be precisely tuned so that the therapeutics can be released at the right time, with the correct dose needed to slow disease progression. In this study, the interaction of NPs functionalized with a cationic ligand, triphenylphosphonium, known to have BBB-targeting capabilities, with several anti-neurodegenerative drugs was characterized and compared to the same formulations without functionalization. A correlation with drug hydrophobicity was found regardless of functionalization, where more sustained release was observed for hydrophobic drugs over multiple days, while hydrophilic drugs experienced a large “burst” release within the first day with trace amounts released thereafter. However, the difference in encapsulation efficiency (EE) between hydrophilic and hydrophobic drugs was not significant. Using the surfactant span-80 during NP synthesis, however, raised the EE of hydrophobic drugs in non-functionalized NPs but had no apparent effect on functionalized NPs, nor on the overall release kinetics for either formulation, regardless of the encapsulated drug. Lastly, the use of surfactant lowered the EE of hydrophobic drugs in functionalized NPs but had no apparent effect on non-functionalized NPs, nor on the overall release kinetics for either formulation. Ongoing and future studies are focusing more deeply on drug-NP interaction properties, surface charge, and cellular internalization efficiency using neurons, microglia, astrocytes and endothelial cells.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Improved Specificity and Sensitivity of CRISPR/Cas12a Using Toehold Modified Crrnas
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Improved specificity and sensitivity of CRISPR/Cas12a using toehold modified crRNAs The CRISPR/Cas (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats/CRISPR-associated) systems, including the most popular CRISPR/Cas9 system, have been used primarily for genome editing applications. CRISPR accomplishes this by utilizing both a Cas protein which acts as molecular scissors as well as a guide RNA which dictates the protein where to cut. Through simple swapping of the guide RNA, different 19-23 base sequences can be targeted for editing. Additionally, a different CRISPR/Cas system based on Cas12a, also known as Cpf1, has been used for both genome editing as well as nucleic acid detection. Cas12a has been recently used for nucleic acid detection by utilizing its single turn-over cleavage of target DNA (cis cleavage) along with a multiple turnover, collateral cleavage of non-specific single stranded DNA (trans cleavage). To quantify the amount of DNA, CRISPR/Cas12a has been combined with Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) based nucleic acid reporters in two different studies named as DNA endonuclease-targeted CRISPR trans reporter (DETECTR) and specific high-sensitivity enzymatic reporter unlocking (SHERLOCK) 1-3 . Both methods rely on recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) to amplify the target DNA to achieve the required sensitivity necessary for nucleic acid detection. Furthermore, they are somewhat non-specific. To address these issues, we proposed making modifications to the 3’ end of the crRNA (CRISPR RNA) that could improve the specificity and sensitivity of the DETECTR or SHERLOCK assay. The method we utilized is the addition of nucleic acids on the 3’ end of the crRNA forming a toehold loop. We hypothesize that by adjusting the length of toehold sequences, the ratio of trans- to cis- cleavage can be significantly altered allowing for an increase in sensitivity and specificity. By adjusting the ratio of trans- to cis- cleavage the toehold loop can be used for either detection (by increasing trans- to cis- cleavage ratio) or specific cutting (by decreasing trans- to cis- cleavage ratio). This will have huge implications for both disease detection and in vivo gene editing utilizing the CRISPR/Cas12a system. Chen JS, Ma E, Harrington LB, et al.
