https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: The Effects of pH and Complexation on Metal Cation Uptake in Nanoparticle Organic Hybrid Material (NOHM) Systems
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The potential use of nanoparticle organic hybrid materials (NOHM) as electrolytes in redox flow batteries is being explored. Redox flow batteries present the advantage of providing large-scale energy storage, beyond the capacity of more common battery types. The most common active material used is currently Vanadium, which is expensive in a pure form, has a corrosive environment, and decreases battery capacity over time. NOHMs are composite particles formed by polymers grafted (either ionically or covalently) onto surface-modified inorganic nanoparticles. Such structure has great potential to capture and carry nonpolar electroactive species. A NOHM comprised of a silica core ionically grafted with polyethylenimine (PEI) polymers is focused on in this study, we refer to this as NOHM-I-PEI. Copper is introduced as a probe to evaluate the effect NOHM structures have on metal cation uptake. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) was used to investigate the electrochemical behavior of the copper species as the concentration of NOHM increases at a fixed Cu(NO 3 ) 2 concentration. NOHM-I-PEI showed inhibition of the oxidation and reduction peaks as the NOHM concentration increased, suggesting the formation of the cuprammonium complex. UV-Vis measurements also suggested the presence of this complex. pH measurements taken for each solution shoed a drastic change along the range of solutions tested. The pH of the solutions was controlled via Britton-Robinson buffers and CVs were ran with this set of solutions. Results from testing these solutions allow for better isolation of the NOHM’s effect from the effect of pH. It is observed that peak intensity decreases as the pH increases. At high pH (>6) complete inhibition is observed, while at lower pH, two cathodic peaks can be seen. Based on these results, it is hypothesized that the bound copper is not available for oxidation/reduction at high pH. Whereas at lower pH, the observed variation in intensity can be related to complexation as a function of the nitrogen to copper ratio. The presence of two cathodic peaks can be explained by the stabilization of the cuprous ion due to complexation.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Development and Modeling of Cu@Ag Core-Shell Nanoparticle Catalysts with Galvanic Replacement for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Efficient solar-driven electrochemical CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR) would provide a carbon-neutral source of fuels and chemical precursors. Copper (Cu) is a catalyst that has been widely studied for CO 2 RR due to its moderate CO binding strength and the variety of products it is able to catalyze. Recent advances in CO 2 RR have made use of engineered nanoscale catalysts with various sizes and morphologies of Cu nanoparticles. One of the main goals of CO 2 RR is shifting selectivity towards C 2+ products, which have higher energy densities and are more profitable when compared to other products. While a Cu catalyst alone produces mostly hydrogen and hydrocarbon products, introducing other metals at the interface changes the interaction between reaction intermediates and surface atoms, enabling tuning of the selectivity. For example, the introduction of silver (Ag) allows for a synergistic effect during catalysis that leads to a shift in selectivity towards oxygenated products, which are not observed with either Cu or Ag separately. Additionally, core-shell bimetallic nanoparticles allow the two metals to be present in close proximity instead of a physical mixture of monometallic particles. Furthermore, the distribution of the two metals can be reliably tuned via a galvanic replacement reaction (GRR). In this work, we present a colloidal synthesis of Cu-Ag bimetallic nanoparticles, employing GRR to precisely control the shell thickness with a diffusion-based self-limiting mechanism. Using Cu-Ag as an example system, we develop a mathematical model based on transport, diffusion, and surface energies that describes the formation of the Ag shell on a Cu core and explains the self-limiting nature of the reaction. The nanoparticles are characterized with bulk composition measurements like ICP-OES and elemental mapping with STEM-EDS to analyze the shell thickness as a function of several reaction parameters. The synthesis demonstrates highly uniform particles with controlled shell thicknesses where colloidal stability is maintained, an important consideration for uniformity when covering the surface of an electrode. The results of the characterization are compared with the model and demonstrate good agreement with experimental results. Since our mathematical model depends only physical material constants, it may be applied to various bimetallic systems to engineer the next generation of nanoscale catalysts and further enhance the selectivity of the CO 2 RR towards desired products.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Synthesizing and Modeling the Optical Properties of Silica Aerogel
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The purpose of this project is to model the optical properties of silica aerogel by solving the 1-D radiative transfer equation (RTE). Silica aerogel is an optically transparent and thermally insulative material with a very low density. Due to its microstructure, which consists of a thing solid backbone of silica particle aggregates enveloping thousands of nanoscopic pores, the material suppresses the three modes of heat transfer. The unique combination of physical and chemical properties allows silica aerogel to be an excellent candidate for solar thermal energy applications. The forward solution to the 1-D RTE will predict the transmittance and reflectance of the aerogel as functions of both scattering albedo and extinction, which are inherent properties of the material. By compiling the numerical results of the forward solution, separate 2-D contour plots can be constructed wherein scattering albedo is plotted versus optical thickness, and the contour gradient represents the theoretical transmittance and reflectance. To determine the intrinsic properties of a specific sample, the transmittance and reflectance of that particular sample must first be determined experimentally using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer equipped with an integrating sphere to account for losses. Once values for transmittance and reflectance are available, the values may be plotted as single contour lines on the previously constructed contour plots which constitute the backward solution to the RTE. When these two plots are superimposed upon one another, it is found that the curves intersect at exactly one data point. This solution point provides the exact scattering albedo and extinction coefficient for a specific sample of silica aerogel. Repeating this process for several samples of aerogel produced by various synthesis processes and with different thicknesses will allow the team to predict the transmittance of a sample synthesized by a specific procedure and of a particular thickness. Furthermore, obtaining the intrinsic properties of a sample will allow for the calculation of the scattering coefficient of that sample, which can be used to determine the approximate pore diameter of the sample. The calculated pore diameter will be verified using Small-Angle X-Ray Scattering. Since the pore size of the resulting aerogel directly affects the degree to which light is scattered throughout the medium, it would be useful to predict the transmittance of a sample characterized by a certain pore size and vice versa; this will indeed be possible using the model formulated in this project.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Light Weight Plasticized Concrete - an Evolution of Sustaining Sustainability.
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Recently, a warning was issued by the UN quoting “World nearing critical point of no return” by 2030 and further debates on sustainable development. Plastic warms the earth twice as much as aviation. Also, plastics are not only polluting but also, they make climate change worse. The most versatile man-made product used in the world is concrete. Concrete uses mainly natural resources like sand, coarse aggregate and fine aggregate, thus depleting these resources exponentially. So, to overcome these major issues we made “SLWP concrete” (The Sustainable Light Weight Plastic concrete). The natural resources like fine and coarse aggregate used in concrete were replaced by 3rd grade waste plastic like HDPE, LDPE, PP, PET in three different variations such as, first replacing coarse aggregate by waste plastic moulds of size 20mm down in two batches (i.e. 50% and 100% by volume). Then, secondly by replacing fine aggregate by waste plastic beads 4.75mm down in again two batches (i.e.50% and 100% by volume) and replacing both fine and coarse aggregate with same combinations. The compressive strength of SLWP concrete showed an increase in strength by 10% and 40% after 7 days and 28 days respectively compared to that of conventional concrete when coarse aggregate was fully replaced. Similar results were obtained when the experiment was repeated with batches of coarse aggregate and fine aggregate too. The results also reveals that of 10%-30% decrease in weight has been observed in SLWP concrete w.r.t conventional concrete. Also, SLWP concrete is economical due to replacement of natural resources by waste plastic. This model was developed with multiple variations to conserve natural treasure and expel the haphazard plastic waste. This method of recovering plastic helps to restore balance in the Eco cycle and to maintain sustainability.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Dynamics of Graphene Sheets at a Water-Vapor Interface: A Molecular Dynamics Study
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Understanding the dynamics of particles at fluid-fluid interfaces has attracted considerable research interest over the past several decades as fluid interfaces create an environment where monolayer thin films can be assembled through a ‘bottom-up’ approach. For example, fluid-fluid interfaces have been used to manufacture highly transparent and electrically conductive thin films of graphene flakes as it has been shown that graphene flakes are thermodynamically favorable at the interface between two immiscible fluids. However, the dynamics of film formation and the interactions between graphene flakes are currently not understood. Furthermore, it has proven difficult to isolate and experimentally probe the dynamics of pristine monolayer graphene flakes at fluid-fluid interfaces. This study aims to address this gap by using computational simulations, which have been shown to reliably estimate real-world experimental scenarios. Molecular dynamics simulations were employed to investigate the lateral interactions and stacking dynamics of mono- and few-layer graphene flakes at a vapor-water interface. Adaptive biasing force (ABF) simulations were used to render potential of mean force profiles and identify different stacking pathways. Additionally, distance versus time profiles were generated for two interacting monolayer flakes and the results were fit according to a power law relation to understand how the interaction pair potential scaled with center-to-center separation distance. Ultimately, this study offers a new perspective into the investigation of interactions between interfacially-bound particles.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Rheology & Thermal Stability of Supercritical CO 2 foams at Different Temperatures and SDS Concentrations
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The use of nanoparticles (NP) combined with surfactants has been a novel practice in the generation of CO 2 foams for hydraulic fracturing. This combination reduces water consumption and formation damage, while improving apparent viscosity and stability of the generated foam. This study evaluates the synergistic effects between nanoparticles and surfactants in CO 2 foams and how surfactant concentration affects the rheology and stability of the CO 2 foam. To assess the rheology and stability of CO 2 foam, nanoparticle dispersion with surfactant is co-injected with high pressure CO 2 at 1500 psi in the CO 2 accumulator and 1300 psi at the system outlet through a bead pack at different temperatures. The generated foam flows through a capillary tube and the pressure drop along the tube is used to calculate the foam apparent viscosity. The heights and texture of the generated foam in the sapphire tube is recorded over time to assess foam stability. To assess the effects of surfactant concentration, the temperature in the chamber is fixed and the concentration of surfactant is changed. To assess the effects of temperature, the surfactant concentration is fixed, and the temperature is changed. From the results, the mixture of nanoparticles and surfactant offered stronger and more viscous foams as compared to foams generated with nanoparticles alone. This is attributed to the synergistic effects between nanoparticles and surfactants, which is believed to form a steric barrier comprised of nanoparticles and enhanced with surfactants at the water/CO 2 interface. The structural integrity reduces the film drainage, the interfacial tension, and film coalescence, which contribute to higher foam performance. The combination of surfactant with nanoparticles in foam generation can offer enhanced foam stability and foam apparent viscosity, which helps maintain foam properties and provide better proppant transport under harsh reservoir conditions.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Peptoid-Functionalized Gold Nanoparticles for Use in Electrochemical Sensors
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Detection of pathogenic organisms is a key part of providing medical care to global communities. Current detection methods are slow, expensive, and sometimes unable to provide the sensitivity and specificity necessary for accurate measurements and effective treatment plans. Electrochemical sensors enhanced with peptoid-functionalized nanoparticles are an alternative to traditional techniques that offers rapid, accurate detection of pathogens. These sensors work by undergoing an electrochemical reaction when their electrodes come into contact with a target molecule; peptoid-functionalized nanoparticle electrode coatings have the potential to increase the speed and specificity of these reactions. Preparation of these modified gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) involves the exchange of stabilizing molecules added during AuNP synthesis for thiol-terminating peptoids designed to provide desired functionality. This surface modification procedure is complicated by both aggregation of AuNPs in peptoid-containing solution and adsorption of peptoid-functionalized AuNPs to polypropylene centrifuge tubes. Successful implementation of functionalized AuNPs in this project requires that no aggregation occurs to limit the functionality of the peptoid or AuNP. Multiple peptoids were observed to cause AuNP aggregation and adsorption, with aggregation rates proportional to the concentration of added peptoid; changes were monitored via visual observation of solution color and solution absorbance measurements. To attempt to delay or eliminate aggregation, solutions were reacted in a variety of different conditions, including the presence of sodium hydroxide or Tween 20, refrigeration, incubation, mixing, and absence of light. Alternatives to an aqueous solution, such as phosphate buffer solution (PBS), were also tested. The identification of a method to stabilize the AuNPs during the peptoid functionalization process is essential to future work on the binding capabilities of peptoid-functionalized AuNPs with proteins found on the surface of pathogenic viruses.

Deposition frequencies (ΔF), dissipation energies (D E ), and viscoelastic behaviors of Z R -ELP were monitored using QCM-D as well. After OTS and ITS SAMs were synthesized, contact angle goniometry suggested that OTS-doped Si-wafers were considerably hydrophobic compared to std. Si-wafers and ITS-doped Si-wafers. https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Development of a Flow-Free Gradient Generator Using a Thiol-Acrylate Microfluidic Resin/Hydrogel (TAMR/H) Hybrid System
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Microfluidic gradient generators have been used to study the migration, growth, and drug response of numerous biological systems including cancer cells and algae. Traditional approaches using serpentine channels produce highly stable gradients; however, these devices require direct flow over the cells, which limits their compatibility with suspension cultures. Flow-free gradient generators have been utilized, but they are often hindered by the need for negative flow or external clamps to maintain fluid-tight seals between the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and hydrogel. The goal of this work was to develop new polymeric materials using thiol-acrylate chemistry to produce a two-layer, flow-free microfluidic gradient generator capable of rapid and facile bonding to maintain fluid-tight channels. The geometry of the device consisted of three parallel channels where a chemoattractant or chemorepellent was flowed through the outermost channel to create a chemical gradient within the center ‘flow-free’ channel. The fluidic channels were imprinted into a rigid top layer, fabricated using thiol-acrylate microfluidic resin (TAMR). The TAMR was bound to a thiol-acrylate hydrogel (H), which served as the bottom layer of the device, and allowed for the flow-free diffusion of chemicals between three parallel channels. The TAMR/H hybrid device consisted of activated acrylate resin made by covalently bonding an amine-curing agent into the acrylate resin coupled with a thiol-containing reagent that is thoroughly mixed into the resin. The hydrogel consists of thiol and acrylate groups within an aqueous buffer. The diffusion of biomolecules through the TAMR/H system and development of a stable chemical gradient was confirmed both experimentally using fluorescent microscopy and computationally using COMSOL. The stability, stiffness, and adhesive strength of the TAMR/H device was thoroughly characterized to confirm proper device operation. The performance of the TAMR/H device was compared to a control PDMS/agarose device with a similar geometry. As proof of concept, the TAMR/H microfluidic device was used to study the chemotactic response of a highly motile strain of GFP-expressing Escherichia coli . The migratory response of both wild type and mutant E. coli was observed in both the TAMR/H and PDMS/agarose microfluidic devices. Population-based analysis confirmed a similarity in performance between the two materials verifying that TAMR/H was a viable alternative to PDMS-based microfluidic devices. These findings highlight the utility of the TAMR/H hybrid system, which has the potential to perform a suite of experiments spanning 3D cell migration and dynamic co-culture between different cell types commonly found in heterogeneous environments like biofilms and cancer.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Formation of Poly(ethylene glycol) Coatings on Silicon Surfaces Via Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Attachment of 4-vinylbenzyl chloride (VBC) monolayers to hydrogen-terminated silicon through UV-induced hydrosilylation generates a surface coating (g-VBC) that can be further modified via substitution reactions at the benzyl chloride moiety. To apply g-VBC in synthesizing functional coatings, we demonstrated the attachment of poly(ethylene glycol) methyl ether 2000 (PEG2000) via nucleophilic substitution. Two reaction systems were used to produce PEG-modified silicon substrates. In the first approach, the deprotonated hydroxyl end of PEG2000 was reacted with surface bound benzyl chloride sites. A variety of reaction conditions were compared to determine those most conducive to high conversion at the surface. In a second approach, VBC was reacted with PEG2000 in solution, and the resulting compound was then grafted to hydrogen-terminated silicon via UV-induced hydrosilylation. For both of these approaches, characterization methods included contact angle measurements to assess wetting and ellipsometry to determine surface thickness. The fouling resistance of the PEG-modified substrates were compared using a FITC-albumin assay to test for non-specific protein adsorption. The developed reaction schemes are of particular interest as they yield Si – C bound films expected to exhibit greater hydrolytic stability than alkoxysilane- and chlorosilane-based methods reliant on siloxane bonds to attach coatings on silicon.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Run-to-Run Reproducibility in Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is a powerful method that can be used to detect analyte interactions on the surface of the working electrode. However, reproducibility issues associated with a repeated impedance measurements of similar conditions using EIS is known. 1 We have identified methodology that can be used to improve the reproducibility of repeated EIS impedance measurements. Multiple factors were taken into consideration for run to run measurement variation such as buffer solution concentration ( e.g. 20mM vs 1 mM ferri/ferrocyanide as a redox couple), buffer solution composition ( e.g. phosphate buffer solution vs. deionized water), and EIS setup options ( e.g. DC offset conditions and N 2 purging). Additionally, techniques such as removing electrodes and rinsing them were tested ( i.e. the working, auxiliary, and reference electrodes were removed and rinsed in between EIS measurements). Some techniques were found to hinder or not affect EIS measurement reproducibility, while others supported reproducible measurements. Taking these methods into account, the most reproducible model of repeated EIS impedance measurements will be discussed. https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Layer-By-Layer Films of Photosystem I and Conducting Polymers
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The integration of Photosystem I (PSI), an essential protein in photosynthesis, into photoelectrochemical cells for environmentally sustainable solar energy conversion has gained attention recently because of the protein’s nearly perfect quantum yield, vast abundance, and nanoscale size. My research examines PSI’s capability to form organic thin films with electrically conducting polymer interlayers. This strategy allows for parts of the polymer to extend into the PSI structure and act as an electron transfer medium between the electrode and protein or between protein layers. I form these films using layer-by-layer (LBL) Deposition, where each molecular layer on the electrode is electrostatically attached to each other by alternating charge. In this case, a layer of PSI containing mixed charge is alternated with a layer of the mixed-charged conducting polymer PEDOT:PSS for up to 10 layer pairs. Film thickness increases by an average of 1.9 nm per polymer layer and 6.2 nm per PSI layer. Infrared spectra are consistent with the presence of both the protein as well as both parts of the PEDOT:PSS polymer in the film. Contact angles were used to assess the composition of the outermost surface of the film after each deposition. Changes in contact angle are consistent with distinct layers adding to the total film for up to ten total layer pairs. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy shows that the polymer entraps ions well to provide minimal change in impedance with increasing film thickness. Finally, photochronoamperometry shows that the photocurrent of the layered films on an electrode increases up to a critical number of layer pairs.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Evaluating the Fluid and Aerodynamic Properties of Uio-66 Nanoparticles
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Pulmonary diseases such as lung cancer, cystic fibrosis, asthma, and chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases (COPD) are associated with alarming annual mortality and morbidity rates [1]. Evidently, current therapies for pulmonary diseases are inadequate, and the seriousness of many pulmonary diseases motivates a need for improved pulmonary drug delivery [2]. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), coordination compounds of metals and ligands, offer promise as nanoparticle drug delivery vehicles due to their cargo-loading capacity, tunable pore size, and potential biocompatibility [3]. The goal of this project is to evaluate relevant fluid and aerodynamic properties of a specific zirconium-based MOF, UiO-66, for drug delivery applications. The cargo-loading, fluid and aerodynamic properties were characterized, while the biocompatibility was confirmed. UiO-66 particles were synthesized under acid-free conditions, with water content, synthesis time, and ligand:metal ratio controlled to modulate the particle size. Using a fluorescent assay, the cargo-loading was characterized for a model cargo, rhodamine B (RB) using particles with varying amounts structural defects, or defectiveness. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) was utilized to measure the hydrodynamic diameter (ZAVG) of particles. The aerodynamic diameter of the particles was characterized using a next generation impactor (NGI), after particles were aerosolized using a collision jet nebulizer. Finally, cytotoxicity was analyzed through a cell titer glow assay after dosing murine-derived alveolar macrophages (MH-S) with particles. The results of SEM yielded geometric radii between 30-120 nm. The median mass aerodynamic diameter (MMAD) decreased from 0.64 μm for unloaded particles to 0.42 μm for max-loaded particles at 7.63% defectiveness. At all other defectiveness levels, a similar decrease was observed. The ZAVG diameter consistently decreased as loading increased across all defectiveness levels. Finally, after dosing alveolar macrophages, no acute toxicity or inflammatory response was observed. The observed decrease in MMAD for loaded particles is an important result, as generational pulmonary deposition depends primarily on aerodynamic particle size. The lack of acute cell immune response after dosage also supports the viability of UiO-66 as pulmonary drug delivery vehicles. References: [1] The top 10 causes of death, Fact sheet N°310. https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Powering Clean Energy with Seawater: Understanding the Selectivity of Oxygen/Chlorine Evolution for Metal Catalysts
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Energy is a globally valued resource. In order to meet energy demands in the face of climate change, finding new methods to store renewable energies is essential. A clean method to store energy is through the electrolysis of water. Such a reaction can be driven by renewable energy sources like solar energy. In this project, an abundant resource is explored as an electrolyte to store energy — seawater. Seawater contains many different salts, often salts containing chlorides. The electrolysis of water evolves hydrogen and oxygen gas, which can act as fuels when recombined in a fuel cell to generate electricity, heat, and desalinated water; however, the addition of chloride containing salts in the electrolyte results in the evolution of chlorine gas, a toxic byproduct, competing with oxygen evolution reaction. The goal in electrolysis of artificial seawater is to understand and control an electrode’s selectivity towards oxygen evolution by analyzing an electrode’s performance via cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry. By comparing the performance of various electrodes, earth-abundant metals with high catalytic activity towards oxygen evolution over chlorine evolution can be confirmed, and a greater understanding of what materials are efficient and selective towards oxygen evolution can be reached. With this understanding comes better electrode designs in the future to improve selectivity towards oxygen evolution. In this project, the tested electrodes have been developed by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, the Epitaxial Complex Oxide Lab from Sungkyunkwan University, and in Dr. Kelsey Stoerzinger’s lab from drop casting and electrodeposition.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Predicting Polyelectrolyte-Micelle Phase Transitions: A Study in Charge Densities
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: In solution, electrostatic complexation may drive oppositely-charged macro-ions to undergo associative phase separation into a complex coacervate phase – a dense, polyelectrolyte-rich liquid with widespread applications across a range of industries — and a dilute phase, the supernatant. The widespread applications of coacervates for molecular separation and controlled delivery have resulted in extensive analysis of the phase behavior and properties of polyelectrolyte-micelle systems. However, much of the work to date has focused primarily on the effects of micellar surface charge density with model polymer-surfactant complexes. Thus, our objective is to explore the effects of stoichiometry and micellar chemistry over a larger phase space, with the goal of constructing a predictive framework for polyelectrolyte-micelle phase separation based on species’ charge densities. Here, we utilize a combination of turbidimetry coupled with optical microscopy to characterize the phase behavior of complexes between the cationic polymer poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDADMAC) with surfactant micelles containing a mixture of the anionic surfactant sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) and the neutral surfactant Triton X-100 (TX100) as a function of composition and salt concentration. Morphology mapping of coacervate formation will help inform future experiments focusing on understanding the effects of both micelle chemistry and polymer charge density. The results from this study will broaden the array of polyelectrolyte-micelle systems for applications such as biomolecular encapsulation and drug delivery.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: pH-Dependent Degradation of Poly(ethylene oxide)- Block -Polycaprolactone Films
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Currently 90% of pharmaceuticals in the discovery pipeline are hydrophobic, yet such hydrophobic compounds account for only 40% of drugs that are FDA-approved and marketable. Consequently, researchers recognize that there is an urgent need for better delivery mechanisms for hydrophobic drugs to increase efficacy and reduce negative side-effects. Poly(ethylene oxide)-block-polycaprolactone (PEO- b -PCL) is an FDA-approved, biocompatible, amphiphilic block copolymer, making it an intriguing candidate for hydrophobic drug encapsulation and controlled release into the body. In this work, a variety of characterization techniques, including DSC, NMR, and SEM, are employed to investigate the degradation of PEO- b -PCL films within aquatic environments. Previous work shows that the degradation of these films is accelerated in both basic and acidic environments, however there are opportunities to better understand the degradation rate as it relates to the physical structure of the films. This information suggests that pH could be used as an external stimulus to guide the release of hydrophobic compounds encapsulated within the PCL. Through examining the effect of block fraction and crystallinity on the degradation rate and pathway at various pH, the potential of PEO- b -PCL as a delivery agent can be better understood.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Development of IL Based Low-Temperature Electrolyte for MET Siesmometer Utilizing Molecular Interactions
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Room temperature ionic liquids (IL), cation-anion pairs that remain liquid at room temperature, have proven to function effectively as electrolytes in a variety of applications, including energy storage devices and sensors. Several unique traits allow for IL to broaden the operating temperature window of the electrolyte. Among these are its wide liquidus range, low volatility, and good thermal and electrochemical stability. The strategy of incorporating other solvents or salts with ILs is broadly applied for enhancements on critical physicochemical properties of an electrolyte. In particular, IL based systems show tremendous potential as electrolytes for the molecular electronic transducer (MET) seismometer to conduct seismology studies under harsh environments. In this work, we present a system consisting of IL, organic solvents, and salt, specifically designed for MET sensing technology at ultra-low temperatures. We discovered that through the formation of hydrogen bonds between the imidazolium cation and the organic solvents, the coulombic attractions between cations and anions are weakened, as evidenced by NMR spectrums. Furthermore, the molar ratio of components in the system has been tuned to optimize the molecular interactions, where neither organic solvent caused undesired first-order phase transitions. This tuned electrolyte boasted a glass transition temperature (T g ) at -119 ˚C, marking the lower temperature working limit of the system. Additionally, experimental results confirmed improvements in fluidity and ionic conductivity over the temperature range of 25 to -75 ˚C when compared to a previously developed aqueous based electrolyte system. Furthermore, the electrochemical stability of the proposed electrolyte is validated to be compatible with the MET sensing technology. Knowledge of the presented work may support the operation of MET seismometers and provide insights for future developments of low-temperature IL based electrolytes.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Immobilization of Laccase on Plantain Fibers for Dye Degradation
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Immobilization process is a commonly used method involving a support used as a structural component and a catalytic component to maximize the properties of both elements and increase the application range. This is a common technique for generation of heterogeneous catalysts. Characteristics of a competitive support for catalyst are affinity, availability and low-cost. In this study, fibers extracted from pseudostem plantain (waste produced by plantain harvests) were used as support for commercial laccase immobilization by adsorption process. Mechanical and enzymatic pretreatments were made to modificate morphology of fiber surface or its superficial area. Laccase adsorption was evaluated through remaining enzymatic activity on fiber, and characterization assays as SEM, FTIR and electrokinetic properties were studied to examine the structural modifications on material surface. Process parameters used during the immobilization (Temperature, contact time and pH value) were analyzed in terms of indigo carmine dye degradation. The change of absorbance was evaluated by UV-Vis. The results showed that a 98 % of degradation was observed after 2 h using immobilized laccase at basic pH values and 5°C of storage temperature. Thus, the immobilization of commercial laccase on plantain fibers is an available strategy for production of low-cost, and functional catalyst for textile industries.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Effect of Functional Groups on the Adsorption of Lighthydrocarbons in Fmj -Type Metal−Organic Frameworks
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Adsorption is considered to be an effective method of light hydrocarbon storage which has advantages in safety and efficiency. Metal − organic frameworks (MOF) , a group of crystalline porous materials with periodic network structure assembled from coordination bond by metal ions/clusters and organic ligands, are considered as promising candidates for light hydrocarbons adsorption due to their highly regulated channel and modified skeleton.The functionalized modification of targeted porous metal − organic frameworks (MOFs) is important to improve the adsorption capacity of light hydrocarbon gases. In this study, five isomorphic MOFs with different functional groups (F,Cl, NH 2 , CH 3 , and OCH 3 ) are successfully synthesized by systematic functional modification of UMCM-151. The differences in affinity of electron effects for light hydrocarbon provide an experimental basis for porous MOFs to improve their light hydrocarbon storage capacity.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Phase Transitions of Titanium Dioxide Nanocrystals
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) is a widely-used catalyst with three distinct nanocrystal phases – anatase, rutile, and brookite. The chemical properties and catalytic activity of TiO 2 vary with its crystal phase, making morphology an important determining factor in catalytic performance. A synthesis method involving thermal hydrolysis of a titanium precursor solution in the presence of urea was implemented for the direct synthesis of anatase and brookite, while rutile was produced through the high-temperature calcination of anatase and brookite materials. The anatase-to-rutile transition (ART) was investigated as a function of both calcination temperature and time to gain an understanding of how those factors affect TiO 2 phase transition. Our results revealed that partial transitions occurred in the 450-550°C range. This temperature range also makes it possible to produce customized mixtures of the anatase, brookite, and rutile phases.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Waste Biomass-Derived Anode for Application in Superior Lithium Ion Batteries
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Given the simultaneous demand for lithium-ion batteries and environmentally-friendly practices, there is a distinct opportunity for batteries derived from waste biomass. Carbonaceous battery anodes synthesized from avocado seeds upcycles a completely valueless waste material into a highly demanded product. The novel electrode demonstrates promising performance, outperforming graphite at every applied current density from 25 mAg -1 to 400 mAg -1 . The novel electrode performs comparably to graphene electrodes in terms of cycling (315 mAhg -1 at 100 mAg -1 ) but does not share graphene’s instability at high (400 mAg -1 ) applied current densities. By characterizing the material using X-ray Powder Diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, BET analysis, and extensive cyclic voltammetry, the amorphousness of the biomass-derived anode was found to contribute 54% of lithium storage to capacitance-driven mechanisms, compared to 35% in graphite and graphene. However, the high amorphousness and high surface area facilitates the formation of a large solid-electrolyte interphase, causing a significant first-cycle irreversible capacity loss. Despite this, its combined superior performance and environmentally-friendly nature causes the presented anode to be a practical upgrade from the current commercial graphite anode.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Computational Studies of the Self-Assembly of Tapered Brush-Coil Polymers in Solution
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Materials formed by the assembly of block copolymers have many applications in environmental cleanup, drug delivery, electronics, optics, etc. In the past, block copolymers with linear architecture have been studied extensively using experiments and simulations. Moving to non-linear architectures, such as star, bottlebrush, and brush-coil, has the potential to advance assembly studies by producing new trends in structure and thermodynamics not seen in linear systems. One specific architecture of interest to us is a tapered brush-coil where the solvophobic polymer block has a bottlebrush architecture of varying density and gradient of side chain length, and the solvophilic polymer block has a linear architecture. In this poster, I will present my recent work, focused on the assembly in tapered brush-coil polymer solutions using a coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulation. For varying grafting density of side chain, gradient, and the direction of gradient of side chain length, I compare the assembled micelle size, aggregation number, and concentration profiles. At low grafting densities, there are observable differences in micelle size between a positive and negative gradient. At high grafting densities the micelle sizes are statistically similar for both gradient directions; however, the chains pack differently within the micelles. This packing is done in a way that does not drastically alter the concentration profile of the micellar core between grafting densities. This implies that while the bulk properties of the micelles may be similar, their internal composition and properties are completely different.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Melting Temperature Effects on the Crystallization Order of PEO-b-PCL Copolymers
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Various samples of poly(ethylene oxide)-b-poly(ε-caprolactone) (PEO-b-PCL) of different molecular weights were dissolved either in toluene or chloroform, melted at different temperatures, and cooled to investigate which block would crystallize first. Depending on which block crystallizes first, it may crystallize more thereby influencing the macroscopic properties of the copolymer film. Analysis was conducted using Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and FTIR. Previous observations have indicated that during evaporation crystallization, the polymer film preferentially crystallizes PCL first but under certain conditions, PEO crystallizes first. These conditions included but were not limited to the solvent used to solvate the film and the molecular weight of each block. So, the goal of this project was to investigate whether the melting temperature influences the order of crystallization of the film. In doing so, the researcher is ultimately trying to find out if it is possible to control the properties of the polymer film.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Residence Time Distribution and Specific Mechanical Energy in Solid-State Shear Pulverization: Processing-Structure Relationships in a Chilled Twin-Screw Extruder
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Solid-state shear pulverization (SSSP) is a continuous polymer processing methodology based on a modified twin screw extruder. The unique application of low barrel temperatures and mechanochemistry have contributed to the development of an extensive range of polymer-based materials, from environmentally responsible polymer blends to nanocomposites, for more than 30 years. The complex processing-structure-processing relationships in SSSP can be elucidated by evaluating the interplay between numerous processing parameters using integrated, measured covariants. Residence time distribution and specific mechanical energy are evaluated in a base case polypropylene study under a full factorial experiment involving screw design, screw speed, and throughput parameters. These factors are in turn correlated to dispersion morphology and thermal property results from a parallel study based on a model polypropylene/carbon black composite. This investigation highlights the tunability of SSSP processing parameters for tailored output with desired purposes and applications. In particular, enhanced residence distribution can be achieved with low screw speed and high throughput settings, leading to high levels of material mixing and shear.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Processing of Nanostructured Block Copolymer Micelle Crystals
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Block copolymers in solvents that are selective to one block form intricate nanostructures that can give rise to useful material properties. The mechanical properties of the crystalline phases seen in concentrated block copolymer solutions depend on nanoscale structure and sample history. In this work, the phase behavior of a triblock polymer, Pluronic P123 (PEO 20 -PPO 70 -PEO 20 ), and water system was studied. These liquid crystals undergo a thermoreversible transition from a liquid-like disordered state at low temperatures (T < 15 °C) into a gel-like soft solid at higher temperatures (T > 20 °C). The goal of this work is to characterize the thermotropic and concentration-dependent mechanical behavior of this system in order to elucidate the nanoscale structures in the P123 and water system and inform future structural studies. We are interested in determining the impact of processing on the nanoscale structure and resulting mechanical properties of these materials. To construct a phase diagram for the P123 and water system, inversion tests were first conducted to distinguish the disordered and ordered states. Samples with visible changes in appearance and viscosity with temperature were identified as target concentrations for rheological study. Subsequent rheometric temperature sweeps were conducted on these target concentrations to locate changes in modulus that may signify structural changes with temperature. Currently, we are working to develop a method to quantify birefringence under shear to distinguish isotropic phases, which exhibit no birefringence, from anisotropic lamellar and hexagonal phases, which are birefringent to different extents. A motivation for this research is the potential application of P123 in drug-delivery systems. Due to its non-toxicity and low-temperature disordering, this polymer could potentially encase therapeutic enzymes throughout the water-filled interstitial spaces. This could facilitate storage of these therapeutic proteins without refrigeration. It is important to understand the impact of processing on these materials so that the desired structures and material properties can be achieved.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Creation of 3D Ordered Superlattices through Self-Assembly of Polymer-Functionalized Nanoparticles
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Functional nanomaterial assemblies are an exciting area of study with various applications across catalysis, photonics, electronics, plasmonics, and biomedical applications. We focused on the study of metamaterials that can show electromagnetic properties not observed in nature with specific interest in their unique optical properties. Using gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) as a model for other metallic nanoshapes, we demonstrated that the respective functionalization of these nanoparticles with poly(ethylene glycol) methyl ether thiol (PEG-SH) and poly(acrylic acid)-thiol (PAA-SH) to form AuNP-PEG and AuNP-PAA core-shell nanoparticles allows for a bridge to be created between neighboring nanoparticles. These bridges were formed through the addition of free polymers in solutions of AuNP-PEG nanoparticles and inter-chain hydrogen bonding between protonated poly(acrylic acid) chains in the shells of AuNP-PAA nanoparticles. We demonstrate that these functionalized nanoparticles self-assemble into 3D ordered structures in bulk solution similar to programmable assembly using complementary DNA strands through the use of synchrotron small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) and various optical characterization techniques. The effect of pH, salt concentration, PEG and PAA chains on the inter-particle distances in the assemblies will be discussed. Facile implementation of block copolymer based self-assembly techniques is enabled by substituting simpler synthetic polymers instead of DNA and the results showed that these superlattices are stabilized by vanderWaals forces, and that allows the structures to be stable even when removed from the aqueous solutions.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Formulation of a Fiber Reinforced Silicon Carbide Colloidal Gel Ink for Direct Ink Writing and Unassisted Sintering
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) is an advanced ceramic material made desirable by its low cost, high hardness, and excellent durability. For these reasons, it is used in a wide variety of applications including ceramic plates in ballistic vests, brake surfaces for cars, and abrasive tools for grinding. However, SiC is susceptible to cracking and ultimately failure due to a lack of plastic deformation, leading to low toughness. Here, a SiC fiber reinforced composite (FRC) material was made into a colloidal gel ink for direct ink writing (DIW) and sintering. DIW enables the fabrication of parts with complex geometries that are difficult or impossible to make with conventional pressing methods, as well as the ability to do rapid prototyping. In this work, 30 vol% SiC whiskers are added to SiC particles to toughen the resulting SiC matrix, while yttrium oxide (Y 2 O 3 ) and aluminum oxide (Al 2 O 3 ) were added in small quantities as sintering aids. The solid ceramic particles were suspended in water using a polyelectrolyte dispersant, and an oppositely charged polyelectrolyte was used as a flocculant. A viscosifier was used to increase ink viscosity and prevent ink phase separation. An ink formulation (>45% by volume solids) has been developed that exhibits shear thinning behavior and has high solids loading. Push-rod dilatometry was used to characterize the densification behavior of the printed part during unassisted sintering. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was used to characterize the microstructure after sintering, and to determine if whisker fracture occurred during ink processing or printing.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: The Study of Segregation of Dyes in PEO- B -PCL
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: As an amphiphilic biodegradable copolymer, PEO- b -PCL is useful for many biomedical applications. The segregation of medicine in the PEO- b -PCL has implication on the release rate of medicine inside a biological system. The objective of the project is to study the segregation of medicine in PEO(5000)- b -PCL(16300) diblock copolymer using azobenzene dyes and bromophenol blue to mimic the presence of the medication. PEO(5000)- b -PCL(16300) films were integrated with methyl yellow, methyl red and bromophenol blue dyes with different mass ratio to determine the effect of dyes concentration on the physical and chemical properties of the copolymer including melting point, crystallization temperature and percent crystallinity of each block. As shown by DSC analysis, the melting point and the crystallization point of PEO- b -PCL both decreased as the concentration of bromophenol blue increased while they both increased as the concentration of methyl red increased. Also, both DSC and ATR-FTIR data showed that the percent crystallinity of PEO block was influenced by the presence of methyl red. However, methyl yellow had no significant influence on the melting point and crystallization point of the PEO- b -PCL. The preliminary results for the dyes segregation in PEO- b -PCL films are: methyl red mostly in PEO block; bromophenol blue distributed among PEO and PCL blocks and methyl yellow stay on the surface of the films.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Thermal Stabilization of Invasion Plasmid Antigen D (IpaD) Using Silica Gels
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The structure of vaccine proteins is vital to maintaining vaccine effectivity; however, exposure to heat can disrupt intermolecular interactions maintaining the secondary and tertiary structures of proteins, thereby making the vaccine ineffective. The cold chain is the system of maintaining vaccine potency by transporting them at constant 2-8°C environment. Unfortunately, it is estimated that 50% of vaccines are wasted before use due to breaks in the cold chain, according to the World Health Organization. Many preservation methods have been applied including entrapment (via sol-gel matrix), adsorption, and covalent attachment. Of these, adsorption has the simplest chemical procedure and does not require harsh chemicals. Silica is often used as an adsorbent due to its porosity, hydrophilic properties, and high thermal stability. Silica is also used in nature to protect organisms from heat denaturation. For example, small organisms such as diatoms and radiolaria are known to wrap themselves in a silica coating for heat protection. Due to these properties, silica has high potential to biomimetically protect and preserve vaccine proteins during transport. Here, we examine the adsorption of Invasion Plasmid Antigen D (IpaD) onto various mesoporous silica gels and study the protein’s increased thermal stability on these solid supports for creating a cold chain independent vaccine. The solution depletion method using UV-Vis is utilized to study the adsorption of IpaD onto silica gels. Then the silica-IpaD complex is heated above the denaturing temperature of the protein to determine if the silica gel maintains the secondary structure of IpaD during heating. These proteins are then removed using N,N-Dimethyldodecylamine N-oxide (LDAO) detergent, and their secondary structure is tested using circular dichroism. The results demonstrate that silica gel maintains a high percentage of the native unheated alpha-helical structure of IpaD, thereby maintaining vaccine potency.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Recyclable Shape-Memory Elastomers
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Shape-memory (SM) polymers are an important class of materials with a wide range of application areas, including biotechnology, textiles, and aerospace engineering. These materials undergo triggered actuation from kinetically metastable deformed states to their original, or permanent, shapes. Semicrystalline SM materials with complete shape-recovery conventionally require covalent crosslinks, thereby precluding melt-processing and recycling. Typical SM polymers are thus constrained to one shape-specific application per product and inherently limited in the sustainability of their life cycles. The objective of this project is to replace covalent crosslinks with strong and reversible hydrogen bonding interactions to enable melt-processable SM polymers without sacrificing performance. Two high molecular weight melt-processable systems have been successfully synthesized, with excellent SM fixities and strain recovery before and after processing. Dynamic mechanical analysis reveals a stiffness plateau that extends over a large temperature range (60-170°C) that is well above the shape-triggering temperature (~50°C). Stress relaxation studies suggest that chain (dis)entanglement kinetics strongly influence the materials’ viscoelastic behavior, including the conditions of temperature and stress under which viscous flow is achieved. Dynamic, time-resolved, isothermal experiments building on these results will better illuminate the relationship between environmental conditioning and stress decay timescales and how it can be used to optimize processing conditions. The role of interchain H-bond strength in determining thermomechanical behavior at high temperatures is also currently being investigated through the use of linkage groups with weaker regimes of interchain association strength.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Gelation of Hyaluronic Acid for Drug Delivery and Tissue Engineering Applications
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a naturally occurring biopolymer found in most vertebrates that regulates cell migration, differentiation, inflammation responses, and angiogenesis. Crosslinking of HA improves mechanical properties and can increase the stability in water, making HA an ideal candidate for drug delivery and tissue engineering applications. Here, methacrylated hyaluronic acid (MeHA) was synthesized to add functional groups for crosslinking purposes and dithiothreitol (DTT) was used to crosslink the HA into a hydrogel. Control of crosslinking of HA in solution yields nanogels suitable for drug delivery, or macroscopic gels useful as tissue scaffolds. A fluorescent tag was added to enable quantification of HA nanogel concentration. Fluorescence spectrometry of samples with varying ratios of fluorescent methacrylated hyaluronic acid (Fl-MeHA) to MeHA revealed a linear correlation between fluorescence intensity and the concentration of Fl-MeHA. In addition, oscillatory rheology was used to determine the stiffness of 3 wt% MeHA gels using various concentrations of DTT crosslinker, and these experiments revealed that gels exhibited varying stiffness over time. These preliminary results show that hyaluronic acid gels have the potential to be used in a variety of contexts including drug delivery and in vitro model systems.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Shape memory polymers (SMP) are smart polymeric materials that can recover from a temporary shape to their permanent shape in response to an external stimulus. In this work, we looked at the effect of process parameters (amount of surfactant, location of surfactant, quench volume, and flow rate) on the polymer nanoparticle diameter produced with impingement jets mixing in a batch-fed process through solvent displacement. Excess surfactant is added to stabilize the polymer nanoparticles in order to prevent aggregation. We find that the quench volume and the surfactant concentration have the biggest effect on polymer nanoparticle diameter and the other parameters have little effect.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Hydrophobic Non-Fluorinated Polymeric Coatings on Cellulose Paper Via Initiated Chemical Vapor Deposition (iCVD)
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Functional polymeric coatings present on materials serve to strengthen surface properties and enhance the versatility of said materials for applications such as packaging, flexible electronics, and microfluidics. While fluorinated polymeric coatings are commonly used for increased hydrophobicity, they can be detrimental to the environment and public health. In this work, we attempt to combat this safety issue by exploring alternative polymeric coatings that boast similar functional benefits to the surface properties of fluoropolymers using a solvent-free vacuum deposition process. Consistent hydrophobicity of the coatings before and after stability tests was confirmed. Hydrophobicities used to demonstrate thermal and mechanical stabilities of PDVB and P(DVB- co -S5) were compared, with P(DVB- co -S5) coatings exhibiting the larger hydrophobicities on both cellulose papers and silicon wafers.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Development of Bio-Inspired Nanopatterned Surface on Polymer Thin Films for Anti-Reflective and Anti-Bacterial Coatings
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Serious infectious diseases from contact with pathogenic microorganisms in our daily lives as well as the fast evolution of drug-resistant bacteria present the urgent need to develop a new functional surface that transcends antibiotics. Recently, physical methods emulating natural, bactericidal surfaces with nanopatterns have been employed in the efforts to combat bacterial adhesion by triggering mechanical rupture of the bacterial membrane. Such biomimetic nanostructures that exhibit antibacterial properties have shown promise in hard materials used for orthopedic implants such as titanium and stainless steel. Yet, little is known about the surface engineering of soft materials to attain bactericidal properties, despite numerous applications of polymers that need prevention of bacterial attachment. We aim to develop antibacterial structures on polymeric surfaces of which conventional benefits from intrinsic materials’ properties are particularly desirable. The main goal of the current study is to develop the biomimetic moth-eye structure on polymer surfaces with both antibiotic and antireflective properties. To achieve this goal, first, we will fabricate the moth-eye mimetic nanopillar-patterned structures on silicon wafers (hard molds) with differing pillar geometries and spacing. By counting colony-forming units (CFU) and live/dead cell assays of gram-negative E. coli adhered on the engineered surfaces, we will find the optimal nano-surface geometry to maximize antibacterial properties. Then, we will obtain the moth-eye mimetic structure on poly(urethane acrylate) that presents a high refractive index by the soft molding pattern transfer technique using a fluoropolymer mold with a very low surface energy. The detailed investigation on the correlation between the surface properties and the antibacterial performance will be conducted to engineer polymeric surfaces for target applications. Development of nanopatterns on polymer thin films to induce bactericidal and antireflective properties will offer a wide variety of polymer coatings for future application in monitors, phone displays, and other optical devices.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Permeability of Cured Composite Skins Produced Using Co-Cure over Honeycomb Core
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Honeycomb sandwich structures made of fiber-reinforced polymer facesheets, film adhesive, and core can be produced using co-cure, during which the facesheets and adhesive are processed simultaneously. Frequently, honeycomb skins (facesheets and adhesive) must be impermeable during service to protect the core from environmental degradation or maintain internal pressure. However, skins can be rendered permeable by process-induced defects such as porosity. This paper describes an investigation of relationships between process conditions during co-cure and skin permeability. Half-sandwich structures composed of a four-ply prepreg laminate, a layer of film adhesive, and a honeycomb core were fabricated using a custom designed lab-scale fixture and controlled thermal and pressure conditions. Autoclave, bag, and core pressures were varied to evaluate hypotheses about mechanisms leading to permeability. Parts were cured with vacuum drawn in the bag and core (resulting in porosity), with super-ambient bag and core pressures (leading to minimal porosity), or with several constant pressure gradients between bag and core (leading to possible continuous flow between these regions). The resulting skins were tested for permeability within a second custom-designed fixture that allowed accurate, repeatable gas flow rate measurements across the skins. Gas flow pathways were also located using a water layer. The micro-structure of the skins was analyzed using light microscopy of polished sections to assess the presence, amount, location, and distribution of porosity and other defects. Results showed that porosity is related to permeability, but that gas flow through skins is possible even without high void contents. Pressure differentials led to complex variations in permeability, showing that variations in gas flow rate between cured skins is at least partly stochastic. Overall, the study contributes to a fundamental understanding of processing and manufacturing science for composites, and can provide useful guidelines for improving manufacturing processes and ensuring part quality.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Adhesion and Shear Modulus in Block Copolymer Gels
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The goal of my research is to quantify the adhesive strength of polymer gels as their molecular connectivity is decreased. Additionally, I aim to identify why such a relationship exists. Polymer gels exist throughout nature; gastropods, such as snails and slugs, produce mucus that helps them adhere to surfaces during their locomotion. Snail slime is so dilute, ranging from 91%-99% water, that it is often used as a lubricant. So, it is scientifically intriguing that it can also function as an adhesive. Thus, we have been analyzing dilute polymer organogels to determine how the decrease in connectivity increases the adhesiveness of the gel. These polymer gels are made of mineral oil and a combination of di-block and tri-block copolymers. As the composition of di-block polymer, in the gels, increases and, correspondingly tri-block copolymer decreases (since their total is held fixed), the molecular connectivity of the gel decreases. Adhesive strength was tested in shear yield-point experiments. Gels composed of 20 wt% total copolymer and 100 wt% to 40 wt% triblock copolymer (0 wt% to 60 wt% diblock copolymer) were using this experimental approach. It was determined that adhesive strength increased as the di-block composition increased while shear modulus decreased. The adhesive strength trend conflicts with that expected based upon qualitative observation. In the future, tests on a series of gels with 10 wt% total polymer composition will be conducted, as well as, alternative techniques explored to validate the observed trends.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Development of a Robust Procedure to Make Non-Swelling, Fast Curing Degradable, Injectable Hydrogels from Thiocure 1300 and Peg 575 Dimethacrylate
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Hydrogels are an important class of biomaterials that consist of a water-swollen polymer. They can be either physically crosslinked or chemically crosslinked. Many chemically crosslinked hydrogels require UV or thermal methods to undergo crosslinking. Injectable hydrogels are hydrogels that can pass through a syringe needle into the body and therefore must either be shear thinning or undergo a reaction in a short period of time to crosslink and form a solid hydrogel once in the body. In 2009, Langer and coworkers developed a degradable injectable hydrogel from poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEG-575-DA) and ethoxylated trimethylolpropane tri-3-mercaptopropionate (ETTMP, Thiocure 1300) dissolved in phosphate-buffered saline at pH 7.5. The two components were separately passed through basic alumina before separately being cooled for 24 h in a refrigerator. Next the ETTMP and PEGDA were mixed together at 4­ °C. Curing occurred within 5 minutes. We tried to replicate this procedure but found no success in making hydrogels. In this work, we developed a robust method to cure ETTMP and PEGDA into hydrogels at pH 7.4 within 2 min. The synthesis of these hydrogel is based on using a calculated volume of precursors that results in an equimolar stoichiometric ratio of thiol and acrylate groups. We varied the height of the alumina column to determine the effect on gelation time. A range of 0.5 in. to 2.5 in. were tested in increments of 0.5 in. Gelation time decreased as the column height increased. A 2.5 in. column resulted in a 1. 33 min cure time and a 1 in. column resulted in a time of 2.3 min. We then varied the pH of phosphate-buffered saline from 7.2 to 7.6. Gelation time decreased with higher pH levels. A pH 7.2 solution cured in 3.32 min. and a pH 7.6 solution cured in 1.38 min. Based on our findings we determined the optimal parameters were a 1.5 in. column and pH 7.4 buffer. This method allows hydrogels to consistently cure in 1.5 min. We then performed a number of tests to analyze the mechanical properties of the hydrogel. Dynamic rheology was used to determine the gelation time, which was confirmed by a frequency sweep to ensure the data was within the linear viscoelastic range. Tensile testing was conducted to verify the elastic modulus of the hydrogels.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Solid-Phase Extractive Polymerization As a New Method for Polyanhydride Synthesis to Limit Oxidation during Polymerization and Improve Purity for Controlled Drug Delivery
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Polyanhydrides are an attractive class of erodible polymer for controlled drug delivery because they can exhibit bulk or surface erosion and they have been shown to stabilize several classes of drugs including macromolecular therapies. The traditional method of polymerizing polyanhydrides is melt polymerization where an activated acetylated diacid prepolymer is heated at 180 °C under vacuum for 1 h to 3 h. The vacuum helps to remove the condensation by-product, acetic acid, generated during polymerization. While this method is effective at producing polymers with molecular weights greater than 15 kg/mol, the intense heating can lead to thermal degradation, oxidation, and discoloration of the polymers. Another issue with this method is the quick increase in the viscosity of the melted prepolymer and growing polymer during polymerization leads to poor stirring and removal of acetic acid. To overcome the drawback of melt polycondensation we have developed a less thermally aggressive method of polymerization that we call solid-phase extractive polymerization. In this method, we use a solvent to facilitate the polycondensation while also extracting the acetic acid by-product with basic aluminum oxide. Using sebacic acid as a model diacid, we studied the effect of a solvent boiling point on the polymer molecular weight. Interestingly, we find that high boiling point solvents allow for temperatures close to that of melt polycondensation but they are not efficient at removing the acetic anhydride because the number of solvent cycles is low. Low boiling point solvents cycle many times but they do not heat the prepolymer enough to get appreciable polymerization. Methylcyclohexane and acetonitrile provide a balance in temperature and number of cycles through the basic aluminum oxide extraction media to produce polymers in the 15 kg/mol to 30 kg/mol range in 1 h. The polymers made with this method also do not exhibit significant signs of oxidation or discoloration. We believe this method may be applicable to many polymerization methods that generate a by-product.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Stability and Kinetics of Phase Transformations of Amorphous Dispersions
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Many pharmaceuticals are composed of two main components: active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) and excipients. APIs are the active ingredients, while excipients are the inactive ingredients. Specifically, in pills/tablets, an API’s characteristics will greatly influence the potency or bioavailability (the ability of a compound to dissolve in the blood to be used by the body). The more bioavailable a drug is, the less is required to achieve a desired effect. Moreover, the structure has a major impact on the bioavailability. The excipient can help to control the structure of the API because whether it is amorphous, crystalline, or some intermediate can influence solubility. Generally, amorphous particles are more soluble and crystalline particles are less soluble. However, crystalline structures tend to be more stable than amorphous structures, and, consequentially, sometimes crystallize fully or partially over time. The polymer excipient helps prevent or slow down this since polymers themselves do not crystalize, so a homogeneous mixture of API and excipient would be expected to have little or no crystallization (Myerson, 2002). The Vibrating Orifice Aerosol Generator (VOAG) helps form amorphous dispersions. These dispersions comprise of a polymer excipient, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), and a model API (a dicarboxylic acid). These are chosen since PVP is a common excipient in many pharmaceuticals and dicarboxylic acids resemble many APIs. Solutions of various weight percents of dicarboxylic acid to PVP are dissolved in isopropanol (IPA). The VOAG works similarly to a spray dryer (commonly used in the pharmaceutical manufacturing): a solution is fed into the machine where it is sprayed, allowing individual drops to dry independently creating small particles. One main difference between the VOAG and spray dryer is that the spray dryer operates at higher temperatures, whereas the VOAG uses ambient temperatures with lower flow rates and improved droplet dispersion to allow for drying. Also, the VOAG produces a narrow droplet distribution which allows the VOAG to create particles of similar size to eliminate size dependency. We form amorphous particles and analyze their dynamic stability. Using powder x-ray diffraction (pXRD), samples are monitored regularly to determine if the particles begin to crystallize, how long this takes, and percent of API crystallization. Standards of known crystallinity are made to compare to the data to determine the percent crystallinity in the sample. This is done using partial least squares regression, peak area, and peak height. References Myerson, A. “Handbook of Industrial Crystallization.” Butterworth-Heinemann. 2002.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The goal of this project is to determine diffusion coefficients for sodium bis(2-ethylhexyl) sulfosuccinate (AOT) reverse micelles through styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene (SEBS) copolymer organogels at varying concentrations of SEBS. Characterizing the diffusivity of AOT through these gels will benefit future applications like transdermal drug delivery through informed structure-property ( i.e. , nanostructure-diffusion) relationships. Previous work in our group has shown that gel nanostructure is tuned by varying the amount of SEBS copolymer. For example, increasing the SEBS concentration increases the size of physical crosslinks and the concentration of chains occupying space in the gel, while decreasing the space between physical crosslinks. The current work uses Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to track changes in gel AOT concentration over time for gels ranging from 10 wt% to 40 wt% SEBS. The acquired data is modeled using Fick’s laws to yield a diffusion coefficient for each gel formulation. The resultant diffusion coefficients decrease with increasing SEBS concentration. We hypothesize that the combination of aforementioned nanostructure trends are the culprit for our observed decrease in diffusion coefficient with increasing SEBS concentration. Understanding the relationship between the gel nanostructure of polymeric organogels and diffusion coefficients of these organogels will provide key insight for biomedical applications.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: FTIR-Based Method for Measuring Diffusion in Organogels
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: In the past decade, various efforts to innovate drug delivery have been developed. The diffusion of nanocarriers in hydrogels has been a common approach. This research studies the diffusion of nanocarriers in organogels, and the results can help similar studies involving both organogels or hydrogels in the future. The main objective of this research project is to develop and validate a method to characterize nanocarrier diffusion in block copolymer organogels. The main driving force of diffusion is the concentration gradient which, in this case, is the difference in the amount of the nanocarrier in the gel and the outside solution. Experiments consisted of three disk-shaped gels each containing 0-1 wt% of a selected nanocarrier. The amount of nanocarrier was measured using quantitative Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) in combination with gravimetric measurements to track gel swelling—both as a function of time. The data was then analyzed by normalizing the peak corresponding to the nanocarrier using the polymer peaks in order to see how the nanocarrier content dropped over time. After running various experiments with a wide range of polymer concentrations and two unique diffusing species, trends on how diffusion can be manipulated were established. For example, higher polymer concentration translated to a slower diffusion rate than low concentrations. Furthermore, unimer diffusion species diffused much faster than nanocarriers ( i.e. , reverse micelles). Ultimately, the proposed FTIR-based method to track diffusion of species in organogels was valid regardless of what polymer concentration or type of penetrant was used. With this information, we can help further the advancement of controlling the rate at which drugs are delivered throughout the body.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Monitoring Temperature Induced Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) Concertation with an Applied Electric Field
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide), or pNIPAM, is a free-radical polymerized polymer, that is commonly studied for uses in surface coatings, tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, biosensing, and more, due to its temperature responsiveness. Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS), used to measure temperature induced coacervation in determining a lower critical solution temperature (LCST), which is typically 30-35 o C for pNIPAM. We initially confirmed the LCST to be thermodynamically reversible and reproducible for both pNIPAM and an electrochemically active poly( N -isopropylacrylamide)- block -poly(ferrocenylmethyl methacrylate) block copolymer, or p(NIPAM- b -FMMA). A voltage was applied through the solution using an electrode lined cell, a technique with DLS that has not been previously reported. We created the cell by inserting copper tape to two sides of a DLS compatible cell, and the leads were connected to a voltage supply to generate an applied electric field across the light path. During the applied voltage, an increase in temperature (“ramp up”) and decreasing in temperature (“ramp down”) was used to look at hysteretic effects on the thermodynamic coacervation. Our results were similar to published values for the LCST of pNIPAM for both increasing and decreasing temperature ramps in the absence of an Applied Electric Field (AEF). However, we observed a decrease in LCST during a temperature increase in the presence in of an AEF (1 V/cm). Additionally, during the temperature decrease, the polymers remained coacervated and were no longer thermosensitive. Upon further experimentation, the same phenomenon occurred from at least 0.4 V/cm and upwards in stepwise 0.1 V/cm increments.
