https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Packing Density and Thermoresponsive Morphology of PNIPAM-Co-PAA Microgel Coatings
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Microgels that alter their size or shape in response to external stimuli such as temperature, pH, and light are gaining considerable attention for their application potential in “smart” membrane technologies. By analyzing microgel depositions on solid substrates, one could better understand how these microgels deposit and function which is critical to advancing their implementation. This study investigates the effects that temperature and pH have on the deposition density of poly[(N-isopropylacrylamide)-co-(acrylic acid)] hydrogels and seeks to find a relationship between density and functional surface roughness change. The microgels were deposited upon silicon wafers primed with poly(octadecene-alt-maleic anhydride) and polyethyleneimine which created monolayer systems. The POMA layer provided a strong base layer due the 18-carbon tail hydrophobic interaction with the wafer. The branched PEI then reacted with POMA’s anhydrides which provided a top layer that was abundant with hydrogen bonding sites for the microgels. Microgels were deposited via spin-coating and incubation at temperatures both below and above the lower critical solution temperature of pNIPAm. Optical imaging and Matlab software were used to determine the densities of the monolayer systems, while a laser scanning microscope and MultiFile Analyzer software determined the microgel surface roughness upon temperature change. As could be expected, temperature and pH played a key role in how the microgel adherence to the solid substrate: increasing temperature and pH showed a positive correlation with density measurements. Following, a relationship was also observed between the density and the temperature associated surface roughness change. Overall, deposition conditions and methods have profound effects on surface morphology that can be qualitatively and quantitively described and related to functional surface roughness change.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Developing Evanescent Wave Scattering As a Tool for Tracking Janus Particle Dynamics in Response to Electric Fields
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Colloidal particles are a highly diverse class of materials that can be observed in numerous applications ranging from ventilation systems to food processing. Colloidal particles can also be fabricated to function as models for more complex systems of biological or mechanical interest to study and characterize their behavior in controlled experimental conditions. Our research focuses on developing evanescent wave scattering as a sensitive technique for measuring small fluctuations in the dynamics of “patchy” and “Janus” colloids with 30% and 50% coverage, respectively. These particles were observed at equilibrium and under the influence of an applied AC electric field. Scattering intensity was analyzed prior to and after application of the electric field to determine what influence this external field had on position and orientation dynamics. Probability distributions were prepared to test the hypothesis that translational and rotational dynamics are influenced by application of an electric field. Due to the characteristic surface coverage of these colloids causing distinct scattering patterns, bimodal distributions in the data were used to suggest unique orientational dynamics. Our results also suggest that a Janus particle will move to a smaller most probable height upon application of an AC electric field.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Production of Monodisperse Yolk-Shell Titanium Dioxide Microspheres with Tunable Characteristics
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Titanium dioxide is a photocatalytic material that has proven useful in the degradation of organic pollutants. In turn, this photocatalyst may prove useful in efforts to handle common greenhouse gases more sustainably. One possible application for the use of TiO 2 in photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants could possibly be a bi-reforming reaction of carbon dioxide and methane into synthesis gas. By degrading these greenhouse gases into synthesis gas, the product gas mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen can be used in the synthesis of hydrocarbon fuels through Fischer-Tropsch reactions. Through this reaction, greenhouse gases may be recycled into useful liquid fuels. Without the use of a photocatalyst, the high reaction enthalpy associated with the aforementioned reforming reaction (247 kJ/mol) renders the reaction non-feasible. However, the implementation of TiO 2 as a photocatalyst may aid significantly in lowering heat energy requirement of the reaction. Unfortunately, the commercially available TiO 2 photocatalyst, Degussa P25, is a mixed phase polydisperse nanopowder with an anatase/rutile phase ratio of 85:15. The high degree of polydispersity coupled with the very small average size of these nanoparticles would result in undesirably dense packing and a high pressure drop across a packed bed reforming reactor which creates obstacles to achieving desirable throughputs at atmospheric pressure. In order to solve this issue, TiO z microparticles with a high degree of monodispersity needed to be manufactured while maintaining or exceeding the specific surface areas of Degussa P25. This work explores the design and production of highly monodisperse TiO 2 microparticles with tunable size, surface morphology, surface areas, and phase ratios. The particles were manufactured in a flow-focusing microreactor composed of three different capillaries that takes advantage of the immiscibility of two feed solutions to create monodisperse droplets prior to the hydrolysis reaction. The continuous phase is a hydrophilic solution containing 1 wt% Pluronic F108 (a surfactant) in formamide, while the dispersed phase is a hydrophobic solution composed of toluene, a photocurable polymer, titanium n-butoxide, and a photoinitiator. The droplets formed by two-phase flow through the outlet capillary are collected in water containing surfactant and subsequently photocured, washed, dried, and calcined. This work has shown that the aforementioned characteristics can be adjusted by varying hydrolysis conditions, precursor composition, and calcination temperatures. In this way, it has been possible to design microparticles suitable for use in photocatalysis of greenhouse gas reforming reactions.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Liquid-Liquid Equilibria Studies of Potential Organic Solvents As Ethanol Extractants from Aqueous Solutions
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Recent years have brought concern for the environment to the forefront, specifically with negative impacts of fossil fuels. Jet fuels are estimated to contribute to 2% of CO 2 emissions and are predicted to rise. Many alternatives to petroleum based fuels are being explored, including biofuels which have the potential to reduce CO 2 emissions by 85%. However, biofuels do not come without challenges. Inevitably, these fuels will have high water content, due to water formed during biological reactions. Unfortunately, water can be damaging to engines, requiring removal for optimum performance rates. Hydrocarbons, such as ethanol, have unideal interactions with water, forming an azeotrope, and cannot be fully separated via simple chemical engineering separations such as distillation, making the process highly energy-intensive and expensive. Liquid-liquid extraction could be a more cost-effective solution, with a proper solvent, because it can be implemented with smaller equipment and lower energy consumption. This project analyzes the effectiveness of using three green, organic solvents: castor oil, dodecane, and 2-methylcyclohexanol, to extract ethanol from water. Liquid-liquid equilibrium was determined using the cloud point method and data for the three ternary systems was collected using headspace gas chromatography at 25°C. A ternary diagram for each organic solvent, water, and ethanol was obtained. Preliminary liquid-liquid extractions using a laboratory scale mixer-settler were used to compare the effectiveness of each solvent in separation ethanol from the aqueous stream. Parameters gleaned from the ternary systems and the preliminary liquid-liquid extractions studies were used to analyze the potency of each solvent in the separation of ethanol. Ultimately, this work provides new insights into the use of green solvents as possible ethanol extraction agents in liquid-liquid extractions processes.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Novel Strategy for Functional Oligopeptide Conjugation inside the Mesopores of Silica Nanoparticles
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The functionalization of mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNPs) with biomolecule-selective oligopeptides is an important method for materials design in bio-separations, drug delivery, and other biotechnology applications. MSNPs are desirable for these applications because their flexible and well-controlled synthesis process provides well-defined pore spaces with high surface areas and pore volumes. MSNPs provide a unique protective microenvironment for binding between target biomolecules and conjugated polypeptides. However, procedures specifically designed for oligopeptide attachment within the pores of MSNPs still need to be developed to avoid uncontrolled reactions at the external particle surface. Here, a functionalization process is described involving a diazirine-based hetero-bifunctional linker, sulfo-succinimidyl 6-(4,4’ azipentanamido) hexanoate (sulfo-NHS-LC-diazirine). This linker allows for controlled attachment of oligopeptides to the surface of the MSNPs (average pore diameter of 8 nm and surface area of 730 m 2 /g) that have been functionalized with amine (-NH 2 ) groups by condensation of aminopropyltriethoxysilane. The choice of hetero-bifunctional linker allows for specific control over whether sulfo-NHS reacts first with the peptide N-terminus or the amine groups on the surface. It is found that peptide-first attachment (reacting sulfo-NHS first with the peptide N-terminus) leads to more efficient conjugation because this approach allows for diffusion of the linker-peptide conjugate to the interior of the particle pores before attachment by UV activation of the diazirine group. This is quantified using the fluorescein isothiocyanate-tagged tetrapeptide arginine-serine-serine-valine (RSSV) to give 0.5 mol peptide/mol amine. To demonstrate the versatility of the approach, three distinct oligopeptides (RSSV, Glycine-Glycine-Glycine-Glycine (4G), and a 16-mer composed of four repeated RSSV units) are conjugated by peptide-first attachment to the surface of the MSNPs. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) shows similar degrees of conjugation for all three peptides, suggesting versatility and generalizability of the procedure developed. Finally, these peptide-conjugated nanoparticles are used as a high-capacity adsorbent for β-estradiol (representative of the broad estrogen family) to show specific binding activity above that of MSNPs without conjugated peptides. This study has implications for utilizing oligopeptide-functionalized MSNPs for bioactive molecule separation from living cells (nanoharvesting) or adsorption for environmental remediation (removal of endocrine disruptors from wastewater).

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: A Bead-Based Microfluidic Testbed for an Enhanced Lab-on-a-Chip Device for Shear Enhanced Purification of Biomolecules
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Protein purification is cumbersome, expensive and requires a number of steps. Post purification, the process equipment often requires extensive, costly maintenance that needs harsh chemicals. Here, we present a new methodology of using shear forces that offers an alternative approach to protein purification that reduces the number of steps, making it easier, greener, scalable and cheaper. Analogous to affinity chromatography, a stationary phase – Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs) - will be used to purify proteins. Protein A will be attached to CNTs using EDC-NHS chemistry. Post attachment, CNT’s will be tightly packed in a microfluidic channel (akin to a packed bed reactor) and are immobilized (against the fluidic drag force) by a transverse electric field from non-planar interdigitated electrodes. At low flow rates, the target proteins (monoclonal antibodies) attach to Protein A while the rest of the solution flows by (filtration). The flow rate is then suitably modified to increase the shear force enough to release the biomolecules from the CNT complex into an elution buffer while maintaining their bio-functionality (purification). Hence, the shear force approach drastically reduces the number of steps required for the desired purification. Post elution buffer, prolonged washing with a solution allows us to regenerate the CNT’s for the next round of purification. To develop optimal conjugation protocols for the process, the whole attachment of protein A to separation has to be done in situ. We have created a testbed with 1 µm carboxylated silica particles to mimic the CNT. Unlike CNT (quencher), silica particles allow us optical (fluorescence) visualization. We have studied in detail the effect of fluid flow, pH, and temperature on the purification efficacy of our platform using fluorescent antibodies. Further the in-situ protocols for EDC-NHS functionalization, antibody attachment and stripping has also been studied using different fluorescent antibodies. The optimization on the silica beads allowed us to translate to a CNT based device which offers tremendous enhancement in shear force among others. We believe that this technology not only benefits the protein manufacturing scene in general (i.e., production of mainstream proteins such as insulin), but also other contemporary, specific applications such as using monoclonal antibodies from cancer treatment to sensors.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Incorporation of Allograft into Chitosan Hydrogels for Treatment of Vertebral Compression Fractures
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: In the United States, 1.5 million osteoporotic fractures occur annually, almost half of which are vertebral compression fractures (VCFs). Currently, the most common non-invasive treatment options for addressing VCFs are kyphoplasty and vertebroplasty. These both include the injection of poly(methyl)methacrylate (PMMA), which is non-biodegradable and has much higher compressive strength than native bone, resulting in an increased risk of adjacent future fractures. We have been exploring chitosan hydrogels as a potential replacement for these established treatments. Chitosan hydrogels have become widely used for tissue engineering applications due to their injectability, biodegradability, and bioactivity; however, poor mechanical properties are an apparent disadvantage of these biomaterials. Recently, a combination of physical and chemical crosslinking (with carbonate and genipin, respectively) as well as physical incorporation of cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) have been shown to produce hydrogels with desirable degradability and low toxicity. Furthermore, incorporation of calcium phosphates into these biomaterials facilitates the release of calcium ions (Ca 2+ ) and phosphate ions (P i ) within their osteoinductive therapeutic window, conveying desirable bone-developing bioactivity. Calcium phosphate incorporation was also found to increase hydrogel compressive strength. Though promising, these hydrogels are still significantly weaker than native bone tissue, leaving them unsuitable for load bearing applications. Recently, we have incorporated crushed cancellous allograft (MTF Biologics) to address this issue. Our results show that these novel complex hydrogels possess physical properties similar to those of healthy bone tissue. In vitro studies will be performed on murine mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) to test the biocompatibility and osteoinductivity of the allograft/hydrogel composite. Additionally, mass loss, swelling, and compressive strength studies will be conducted to ensure that the hydrogels have desirable ion release profiles and mechanical properties for VCF repair applications. It is expected that these complex hydrogels will have the same osteoinductive properties as the original hydrogels while also having the improved strength necessary to support load bearing bone regeneration.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Graphene Oxide Membranes: Synthesis Methods, Unique Properties, and Potential for Perfluorooctanoic Acid (PFOA) Removal
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) creates a thin membrane with tight interlayer spacing that allows it to maintain high permeability along with high particle selectivity. A GO membrane was created using a vacuum filtration cell to cast a dilute, aqueous solution of graphene oxide onto a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF200) substrate. A GO membrane with a 33% decrease in graphene oxide loading showed decreased membrane thickness, increased permeability, and decreased rejection of dextrose molecules suggesting that the incidence of defects increased when GO loading was reduced. The graphene oxide adopted a negative charge at any pH above ~3.5 and exhibited a maximum negative zeta potential of -22.5 mV at pH=8.2. Graphene oxide’s negative surface charge in neutral water, improves its rejection of negatively charged particles such as perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) by charge repulsion. PFOA is a harmful, biologically persistent compound that contaminates water supplies, particularly near chemical plants where it is manufactured or disposed of. PFOA rejection was found to be highest in a high pH solution with a low PFOA concentration. The GO membrane rejected 58% of a 20-ppm PFOA solution in distilled water (pH=7) but rejection increased to 75% when a 1-ppm PFOA solution was used in the same conditions. It is predicted that lower concentrations of PFOA, like those present in drinking water, could achieve near complete rejection. When a lower pH solution (pH 3) was used, the retention appeared to be nearly as high, but the “rejection” proved to be entirely due to adsorption on the membrane surface based on a large disparity in the mass balance. PFOA rejection dropped to 15% when tested in a 90/10 isopropanol solvent with 1 ppm PFOA concentration, suggesting that charge plays a major role in rejection.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Non-Enveloped Virus Purification Using Cation Exchange Chromatography
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The supply of vaccines is not consistent and can leave countries without access to lifesaving vaccines. Companies are leaving the market due to multifactorial production issues which leaves countries without access to vaccinations. Vaccine manufacturer’s ability to make pure and potent vaccines depend directly on the capability to purify viruses without a decrease in yield. Currently, chromatography is the most common method in industry to purify bioproducts because of its versatility. The mode that is most used for viral purification is ion exchange chromatography. Currently, anion exchange chromatography (AEX) is used more often in virus purification. AEX allows negatively charged viruses to bind to a positively charged chromatography surface at neutral pH, where viruses are the most stable. However, cation exchange chromatography (CEX) has the potential for improved purity. All forms of chromatography share the same basic steps: equilibration, loading, elution, washing, and regeneration. CEX uses two forms of elution, increasing salt gradients or increasing pH gradients. The more common of the two is the salt gradient because of its simplicity and reliability. However, virus elution yields are often low with salt gradients due to the variability of the viral surface. Gradients using a change in pH exploit the biomolecule’s isoelectric point (pI). pH gradients are more complex to design but have the potential to provide the necessary separation to rapidly purify vaccine products. The non-enveloped virus porcine parvovirus (PPV), with a reported pI of 5, was purified with CEX. PPV was loaded at pH 3.5 and eluted with a pH step gradient. High recovery of virus particles was found during the elution step of pH 6 with high concentration of the virus eluting over the duration of the pH 6 step. Purity analysis demonstrated a removal of 92% contaminating protein and 98% DNA. Future work will comprise of purification of different viruses and increasing loading volumes to concentrate products. This research will result in improved methods of purification that will bring new vaccines and gene therapy vectors to market and keep costs low.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Green Solvent Extraction of Soy Biomass
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Biofeedstocks contain a variety of components that can be used as fuels or as value-added chemicals and are of particular interest in the energy, pharmaceutical, and nutraceutical industries. Solvent extraction is a useful and well-developed means of extracting many of these components. Because solvents account for a considerable portion of process waste, it is important that green solvents (solvents with fewer environmental, health, and safety impacts), are used to extract these products . In this work, a variety of green solvents were used to extract triglycerides and phospholipids from two biofeedstocks, soy lecithin and soybean flour . The components in each extract were analyzed using supercritical fluid chromatography-mass spectrometry in order to determine the extraction efficiency and selectivity of each solvent. Overall, it is seen that certain solvents, such as acetone and ethyl acetate, were more selective towards triglycerides than phospholipids while other solvents, such as 2-methylhudrofuran, were more selective towards phospholipids than triglycerides. These results make it easier to select a particular solvent when carrying out a solvent extraction based on the yields of the component needed in an extract. In addition, this work analyzes the properties of each solvent to allow for predicti on of the effectiveness of other solvent s with similar properties in order to aid in the selection of solvents for extraction processes.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Per - and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and related compounds such as perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) are labeled as persistent organic pollutants by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). PFAS were used in firefighting foam, non - stick cookware, waterproof outdoor gear, food packaging , and more. PFAS have contaminated the drinking water supply of many countries around the world, including the US . Acc ording to the EPA , PFAS accumulate and stay in the human body for l ong periods of time and are harmful to the body’s reproductive and immunological systems . In 2019 , the EPA recommends PFAS levels of no more than 70 ppt in drinking water and million s of people in the US are regularly drinking water contaminated with more than this level . There is a need to effectively and efficiently remove PFAS compounds from drinking water. Currently g ranular activated carbon and i on - exchang e/non - ion - exchange polymers in the form of resin beads are used to adsorb PFAS from water in water treatment plants . T he se methods u tilize diffusive flow to adsorb PFAS which is a slow process . Nanofiltration and reverse osmosis can also be used to remove PFAS from water but are expensive to perform due to pressure requirements . If membrane adsorbers utiliz ing convective flow were able to effectively capture PFAS from water they would enable a new treatment technique for PFAS mitigation. This would allow th e adsorption of PFAS to be regulated by slightly pressurizing the contaminated water to pas s it through the membrane, resulting in a more efficient method of purification . Polyethersulfone membranes w ere utilized to remove sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) , a surrogate of PFAS, from water . UV photopolymerization w as utilized to graft a polymer layer from the membrane surface . 2 - [( m ethacryloyloxy)ethyl]trimethylammonium chloride (MOETMA), 2 - ( d imethylamino)ethyl methacrylate (DMAEMA) , 4 - v inylpyridine, and b utyl a crylate (spacer molecule) were the polymers experimented with. The membranes were tested with and without the addition of a cross - linker , m ethylenebis(acrylamide) (MBAA) , which acts to stabilize the adsorbing polymer chains on the surface of the membrane. B romoethane was used to quaternize poly( 4 - v inylpyridine ) . The positively charged polymer chains allow ed the membrane to adsorb the negatively charged SDS from solution. Each membrane was flux tested to determine if modification was successful. ATR - FTIR spectroscopy w as used to determine the extent of modification. C ontact angle goniometry w as used to determine the effect of modification on the hydrophilicity of the membrane. Static adsorption testing was done to determine the membrane adsorption capacity for SDS.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Comparing the Efficacy of Enveloped Virus and Non-Enveloped Virus Purification in Aqueous Two-Phase System
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The existing need of viral vaccines in the less developed regions and growing demand for gene therapy vectors and oncolytic virus therapy has demanded the biopharma companies to upgrade the current production strategies. Downstream processing to purify viral particles from the host cell contaminants is one of the major contributors to not only limiting the throughput but also cost of vaccine production. Current methods based on chromatography and filtration are facing a major challenge to meet the required high yield production. Aqueous two-phase system (ATPS) has been identified as one of the potential candidates to address these issues in the vaccine manufacturing. ATPS formed by two partially miscible aqueous solutions can be composed of polymer-polymer or polymer-salt. However, the discrepancy in understanding the biomolecule partitioning mechanism has stalled the industrial implementation. Our previous study with porcine parvovirus, a non-enveloped virus, has inferred that two major forces, hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions, drive viral particles and contaminant proteins to the opposite phases in a polyethylene glycol (PEG, MW 12000 Da) and citrate salt system. This work explores the purification of structurally different category of viruses than the previous study to generalize the notion of above-mentioned driving forces and reduce the experimental space to optimize the purification. This study used model enveloped virus (herpes simplex virus, HSV-1), which has an extra bilipid membrane around the protein capsid enclosing the genetic material. The recovery of the virus in the PEG-rich phase was studied with an increasing PEG and citrate concentrations at various tie line lengths to study the partitioning behavior of viruses. Further, water structure amending compounds, osmolytes (glycine, betaine, and TMAO), were included in the system to compare the enhanced driving forces to boost the purification at lower compositions. The results from our experiment can be used to provide higher virus recovery and help lower overall vaccine production cost .

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Pressure swing adsorption (PSA) has the potential to be used for post-combustion CO 2 capture, as well as CO 2 capture from other gas sources. However, carbon capture based on adsorbent equilibrium selectivity is not viable with basic PSA cycle scheduling since recovery of reasonably pure CO 2 requires pressure ratios which are unrealistically large and expensive. https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Aminopropylsiloxane Networks for Regenerative Carbon Capture Sorbents
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: With over half of the world’s energy generated from the combustion of fossil fuels, the demand for developments in carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) capture technology has surged over the last decade. The end goal for captured CO 2 is to utilize it by chemically converting it into value-added products. Currently, amine sorbents are the most prominent and effective mechanism for sequestering CO 2 at both high and low concentrations. Historically, liquid amines have been used for adsorption of CO 2 from flue gas on the commercial scale. However, aqueous sorbents capture CO 2 by the physical formation of bonds (physisorption), therefore requiring more energy to regenerate the sorbent compared to a solid sorbent that adsorbs CO 2 by chemisorption. Currently, research efforts are focused on increasing the adsorption capacity of solid materials in order to be cost-efficient and comparable to that of aqueous capacities. Here, a silica-supported, solid sorbent was functionalized with propan-1-amine groups using aminopropylsiloxane networks. Nitrogen loading on the sorbent was measured using a LECO elemental analyzer. Absolute CO 2 adsorption capacity was obtained by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Monolayer uptake measurements, corresponding to active surface area of the sample, were taken by a Quantachrome Gas Sorption Analyzer. Monolayer uptake and nitrogen content were compared to gain an understanding of the aminopropylsiloxane assembly and active site availability to incoming gas. Thermal cycling stability of the sorbents was also characterized using TGA to test the sorbent’s ability to regenerate active surface area upon CO 2 desorption. These solid sorbents are considered “low temperature” with adsorption and desorption steps both occurring at temperatures lower than 200°C. Sorbents with different mass loadings of nitrogen and varying functional group length were analyzed and compared.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Self-Regulating Forward Osmosis-Reverse Osmosis Hybrid System
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Self-Regulating Forward Osmosis-Reverse Osmosis Hybrid System Colin Fitzsimonds, Noah Ferguson, Dr. Jeffrey McCutcheon Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, University of Connecticut, Storrs, CT Although reverse osmosis (RO) is a commonly used desalination technology, the susceptibility of these membranes to foul makes them challenging to operate in wastewater reuse applications. Pretreatment of these feed solutions is one method of reducing the fouling of RO membranes. Such systems often significantly increase the footprint of the desalination plant and the CAPEX for construction. Using forward osmosis (FO) as a pretreatment method in a hybridized system has been considered as an alternative method to dealing with difficult to treat feed waters. The potential complexities to balancing the fluxes between the FO and RO systems and overall uncertainty about the operation of these systems act as a deterrent to their use in a desalination plant. In this work, we demonstrate self-regulating behavior that could allay fears of needing complex process control regimes in these types of hybridized systems. We demonstrate this behavior using a module-scale testing system that mirrors the behavior of a larger scale system. The system shows flux convergence between the FO and RO modules when disrupted by a sudden change in the RO module pressure and therefore does not require complex controls to ensure flux convergence between the two processes.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Temperature Swing Adsorption of Perfluoroorganics By Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) Hydrogels and Membranes
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: This research is aimed at evaluating the effect of temperature on the removal of perfluoroorganic compounds in water filtration. Polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) microfiltration membranes are functionalized with poly-N-isopropylacrylamide (PNIPAAm), and its temperature responsive behavior is studied as it relates to water flux and adsorption/desorption of perfluorochemicals. PNIPAAm has a relatively low Lower Critical Solution Temperature (LCST) of around 32°C, which makes it appealing for industrial use. PNIPAAm has a sharp transition from hydrophilic behavior below its LCST to hydrophobic behavior above its LCST, thus, when the PNIPAAm is exhibiting hydrophobic behavior, it retracts/collapses upon itself in an aqueous environment. In doing so, the isopropyl groups dehydrate first, causing the polymer chain to collapse, thus causing hydrophobic contaminants to partition into that domain. Reversely, bringing the temperature down past the LCST will rehydrate the isopropyl groups, which reduces adsorption and allows desorption to occur. The stability and reusability of these membranes are demonstrated as well. Specifically, this study’s goal is to evaluate the feasibility of temperature swing adsorption/desorption of Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in water filtration. This research is supported by the NIEHSSRP grant P42ES007380, and by the NSF KY EPSCOR program. Full-scale PVDF membranes were developed through collaborative work with Nanostone-Sepro (Oceanside, CA, USA).

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Low-Cost Microfluidic Devices for Bio-Separation Applications
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Single-use vessels have gained significant popularity in the biological processing industry. In this work, we develop software and process equipment for manufacturing a single use or recyclable separation device for the extraction of DNA from solution. Additional software is developed to control the extraction process. Separation units consist of submillimeter expansion-contraction channels, fabricated from machined thermoplastics using a low-cost (<$200) micro-mill. The mill is controlled by a Raspberry Pi, running a homebrew Python code which generates and streams commands to the mill. The separation of DNA from solution is achieved by Electrohydrodynamic Migration, in which DNA molecules are stretched into cigar-shaped conformations by the shearing forces generated by the Poiseuille flow, with the long axis tilted towards the center of the confining channel. An electric field, applied counter to the flow, then has the effect of selectively driving the DNA towards the channel walls. Near the walls, the motion of the DNA is dominated by electrophoresis, which returns the molecules to the inlet of the device. The process leads to a selective concentration of DNA in a small region around the beginning of the contraction. Separation and concentration require precise control of the applied voltage and pressure differences which are achieved by Arduino microcontrollers controlled via serial connections by a Python interface. Using Python for experimental control allows for reproducible experiments, by saving the controlling instructions as ladder logic in text files. Additionally, the Python interface allows for real-time analysis of the images gathered by the microscope camera, which can be used to fine tune the experiment via application of feedback controls.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: The Effect of Calcination Extent on Sorbent Utilization in Calcium Looping
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Calcium looping is a promising carbon capture technology, circulating CaO-based sorbents between carbonator and calciner units. Natural limestone is a popular choice for the sorbent material due to its abundance and low cost. However, rapid sorbent deactivation is a major challenge to the long-term stable operation of the calcium looping system. Previous studies have mostly focused on the decay of utilization of fully calcined sorbents over multiple cycles of carbonation/calcination. However, lime-based sorbents are rarely fully calcined in practical operations and, hence, the effect of partial calcination on sorbent cyclic performance is of interest. This work investigates the effect of the extent of limestone calcination on sorbent utilization decay over multiple cycles. Greymont limestone particles (510-700 µm in diameter) were calcined and carbonated for 20 successive cycles in a thermogravimetric analyzer (TGA). The extent of calcination was varied by changing the calcination time, with the calcination time being fixed for each cyclic test. It was observed that partial calcination results in enhanced sorbent utilization over the testing cycles. The experimental results give better understanding of the mechanism of sorbent utilization decay, while also providing more experimental support for prospective calcination kinetics modelling. Future study will verify the observed effects of partial calcination for prolonged numbers of cycles and different calcination operating conditions.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: The Modeling and Measurement of Solute Solubility and Partitioning for a Hybrid Supercritical Fluid/Ionic Liquid Extraction Process
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Chemical separation is an important aspect of chemical engineering, and many techniques for these processes are large energy sinks and produce a lot of waste. Ionic liquid enhanced supercritical fluid extraction is one way to reduce both the energy required and waste produced. Ionic liquids (ILs) are organic salts that have a melting point of 100°C or below and have practically no vapor pressure. Supercritical fluids (SCF) are compounds that are above both their critical temperature and pressure. These compounds have gas-like transport properties and liquid-like solvation properties. Both ILs and SCFs can be tuned to perform specific tasks. IL’s ions can be modified by changing the functional groups to alter certain properties like solvation affinity for desired compounds, thermal properties, and physical properties such as density and viscosity. SCFs can be modified by changing temperature or pressure to attain transport or solvation properties that are more like a gas or a liquid, respectively. IL enhanced SCF extraction utilizes these properties to create a separation technique that may be able to selectively separate a mixture into its base compounds. The current project is to demonstrate this separation technique by utilizing the Peng-Robinson Equation of State with Van der Waals mixing rules to model the solubility of different dyes in the SCCO 2 to determine the pressure needed to ensure the maximum amount of solubility within reason. Preliminary experiments have been conducted to transfer dye from a solid mixture to an IL and from a dye-saturated IL to a pure IL. All experiments conducted have supported the hypothesis that SCFs can be used to as a pathway to transport compounds from solid/liquid to another IL. A computer program, COSMO-RS, has been utilized as a screening method to analyze ILs and various dyes to calculate the activity coefficients of the ionic liquid. This allows a partition coefficient to be calculated and a combination of dye/IL to be selected to use in upcoming experiments. The current goal of the work is to selectively separate two different dyes into two different ILs, using disperse dyes as model compounds to demonstrate the utility of non-contact separation. The eventual goal, however, is to move from dyes to more practical implications such as extracting pharmaceutical compounds using this method, improving separation techniques in the chemical engineering industry.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Fabrication of a Novel Reactive Membrane for Degradation of Polyfluorinated Compounds
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Nanomaterials are typically used in the field of membrane technology to impart a desired characteristic on the membrane so as to enhance selectivity of the membrane and increase the life span of the membrane. Photocatalytic membrane processes generate oxygen-reactive radicals under irradiation by light that could degrade pollutants in feed solutions. Phosphorene is a recently discovered two-dimensional material that shows great promise as a photocatalyst because it can generate reactive oxygen species (singlet oxygen, hydroxyl radicals and superoxide radicals). The main objective of this collaborative research is to develop and validate environmentally safe nanomaterial-based approaches for treatment of drinking water including degradation of per- and polyfluorinated chemicals (PFAS). PFAS are surfactant chemicals commonly found in household and commercial products, but they are also very persistent in the environment and are known human carcinogens. They are very resistant to traditional drinking water treatment technologies and hence a reactive membrane that can degrade and remove these harmful chemicals during the treatment process will be worthwhile. Specifically, we aim to study the in vivo toxicity of phosphorene in its free form and in filtrates after nanoparticles are embedded into the membrane on C. elegans mortality, reproduction, behavior and antioxidant responses. Among PFAS that will be used, are representatives of long-chain PFAS including perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluoroheptanoic acid (PFHpA), and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) as well as newer short-chain PFASs, such as GenX. In this research, phosphorene will be fabricated by the liquid exfoliation of black phosphorus. Membranes will be made via the non-solvent induced phase separation technique. Phosphorene will be physically incorporated into the membrane. The membranes will be characterized using several microscopic and analytical techniques and finally tested for the degradation of PFAS in solution.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Towards Fractionation of Soybean Meals in a Water- and Chemical-Free Environment
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Traditional wet fractionation techniques have many drawbacks due to the utilization of acid, alkali and chemicals which cause denaturation and, consequently, loss of protein solubility. In addition, plenty amount of resources such as water and energy are required to produce protein isolates using wet methods. In contrast, dry separation processes such as air classification, sieving and tribo-electrostatic separation preserve native functionality of proteins. The aim of this research is to implement the novel tribo-electrostatic separation technique for the production of protein-rich and fiber-rich fractions from defatted soybean ( glycine max ) flour followed by optimizing the separation operating parameters. The tribo-electrostatic separation is based on the phenomena that proteins have better chargeability properties than carbohydrates. This can be explained by the presence of many ionizable groups in proteins such as amine groups, carboxyl groups and side chains. Our custom-built separation unit including a tribo-charging tube, separation chamber with two oppositely charged electrodes, and fluidized bed was implemented in the Bioprocess Engineering Research Laboratory at Howard University. In this study, soybean particles were first charged in the charging tube and then separated in the fractionation chamber based on the acquired charges under the influence of external electric field. The optimization of process parameters was performed. We tested two different air flow rates (7LPM and 15LPM) and three plate voltages (±1kV, ±3.5kV, and ±6.5kV). At the most optimal processes conditions, the initial protein and fiber contents of soybean flour were increased from 55.3% and 15.3% to 58.4% and 19.6%, respectively. These accounted for 66.5% of the total protein and 60.8% of the total fiber. This novel technology is water-free, chemical-free and eco-friendly alternative to the traditional wet protein separation methods.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Monoethanolamine Based DES for CO 2 Absorption: Insights from Molecular Dynamics Simulations
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Several ionic liquids have been designed to absorb CO 2 and thereby decrease greenhouse gas emissions. Among them, novel deep eutectic solvents (DESs), with their commercially attractive properties, have recently been studied for CO 2 capture process. In our previous work we have studied molecular structure of DESs composed methyltriphenylphosphonium bromide (MTPPBr) and mono ethanol amine (MEA) at molar ratio 1:6, 1:7 and 1:8, which are known to have high CO 2 absorption capacity. In current work, we analyze interactions between above mentioned DESs and CO 2 using molecular dynamics simulations to understand CO 2 absorption process. Results based on interaction energy and radial distribution functions (rdfs) have shown strong interactions between MEA/Br and CO 2 suggesting the capture of CO 2 by these compounds. Additionally, low diffusion coefficients of ions suggest high viscosity of DESs, an impediment to its commercial development. Water was added to DESs in different amount, to analyze the influence of water on to DESs’ viscosity. Results show that structure of DESs remains same up to 50% of water in DESs, while viscosity of DESs starts to decrease significantly above 50%. For same purpose, DESs were also examined at higher temperature that lead to significant decrease of viscosity. Taken together, work assists in understanding interactions between CO 2 and DESs’ component and CO 2 absorption mechanism, additionally it suggests methods to decrease DESs viscosity, along with optimized process conditions, for further industrial implementation.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Residence Time Distribution and Holdup in Centrifugal Extractors
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Annular centrifugal extractors (ACE) are liquid-liquid extractors which achieve high extractive efficiencies with a fast residence time. However, due to a fundamental lack of understanding of the driving force and the kinetics of ACE units, scale-up is, currently, not feasible. This study seeks to quantitatively understand the hydrodynamics of the ACE units through phase holdups and residence time distributions (RTD). Ultimately, data from this study will help build mathematical models to improve the physical description of the system. To experimentally determine RTD and holdup, organic (30% tributyl phosphate in isopar) and aqueous (0.0071% nitric acid solution) streams were brought to steady-state through a 4-pack extractor unit. Then, Sudan I dye was added to the inlet organic stream, and concentration data was collected over a 10-minute period from the organic outlet stream. Subsequently, RTD and holdup were quantitatively calculated with the concentration data.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Time-Dependent FTIR Microscopy for Mechanism Investigations and Kinetic Measurements in Interfacial Polymerisation : A Microporous Polymer Nanofilm Study Dan Ren 1 , Jet Ing Ngie Yeo 2 , Tian-Yin Liu 1 ,2* and Xiaolin Wang 1* 1 Beijing Key Laboratory of Membrane Materials and Engineering, Department of Chemical Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China 2 Barrer Centre, Department of Chemical Engineering, Imperial College London, South Kensington Campus, London, SW7 2AZ, UK *email: *tianyin.liu@imperial.ac.uk * xl-wang@tsinghua.edu.cn Interfacial polymerisation plays a pivotal role in chemical industry and academic researches but acquiring chemical insights into the formation of ultra-thin films remains challenging. [1] A real-time and in-situ characterisation of the interfacial polymerization process is demonstrated here by using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR)-mapping spectroscopy with microscopy. The entire formation process of microporous polyarylate films was studied using this approach to reveal the mechanism and measure reaction kinetics, which are not established. Our key findings reveal that the mechanism involves a two-stage reaction: the diffusion-controlled stage and the film formed stage. We measured the diffusivity by 2D- DOS Y of 1 H-NMR and the oil/water partition coefficient K by UV spectrum. The concentration changes of each species over time is quantified based on areas of the identified FTIR peaks. The reaction rate constant, k is obtained for resorcinol (RES ) - trimesoyl chloride (TMC) (119.0 L mol -1 s -1 ) and 9,9-bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)fluorene (BHPF)-TMC (32.87 L mol -1 s -1 ) ,which illustrated that the rigid and contorted monomer, BHPF, is slower in both diffusion and reaction during film formation. https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Direct CO2 Capture from Air Using Poly(ethylenimine)-Loaded Polymer/Silica Fiber Sorbents
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Direct CO 2 capture from atmospheric air is gaining increased attention as one of the most scalable negative carbon approaches available to tackle climate change if coupled with the sequestration of CO 2 geologically. Furthermore, it can also provide CO 2 for further utilization from a globally uniform source, which is especially advantageous for economies without natural sources of carbon-based feedstocks. Solid-supported amine-based materials are e ff ective for direct air capture (DAC) due to their high CO 2 uptakes and acceptable sorption kinetics at ambient temperature. In this work, we describe the application of polymer/silica fi ber sorbents functionalized with a primary amine-rich polymer, poly(ethylenimine) (PEI), for DAC. Monolithic fi ber sorbents composed of cellulose acetate and SiO 2 are synthesized via the dry-jet, wet quench spinning technique. These fi bers are then functionalized with PEI (M w 800 Da) in a simple and scalable postspinning infusion step and tested for CO 2 capture under pseudoequilibrium conditions as well as under breakthrough conditions. An investigation to study the e ff ect of feed fl ow rate, adsorption temperature, and presence of moisture in the feed on the CO 2 breakthrough performance of a densely packed fi ber sorbent module is conducted to highlight the potential application of this class of structured contactors in direct air capture. The pressure drop of these contactors at high gas velocities is also evaluated. Finally, a vacuum-assisted desorption step is demonstrated for production of high-purity CO 2 from both dry and humid ambient air mixtures.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Ionic Liquid Enhanced Supercritical Fluid Extraction
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Ionic liquid enhanced supercritical fluid extraction (ILESCFE) is a novel, environmentally benign extraction process that carries the potential to be a widely applicable, tunable alternative to traditional extractions. Traditional extractions rely heavily on volatile organic solvents which are often toxic and can easily escape into the environment as fugitive emissions. ILESCFE eliminates the issue of fugitive emissions due to the fact that the supercritical fluid (SCF) is environmentally benign and ionic liquids (ILs) effectively lack a vapor pressure. The properties of the SCF can be tuned by slight adjustments to temperature and pressure and ILs can be tailored to specific tasks through the addition of different functional groups and by using different cation-anion pairs. ILESCFE operates under the 0 th Law of Thermodynamics to accomplish no-contact in situ concentration of the solute into the desired ionic liquid. Systems of multiple ionic liquids can be designed to achieve high selectivity of the desired solute in an extraction. This research focuses on modelling with COSMO-RS which is a quantum chemistry-based method that can predict the behavior (activity coefficients) of species in a mixture. COSMO-RS can be used to quickly screen countless ionic liquids to determine which ILs exhibit the proper selectivity for a given solute. Preliminary screening has indicated efficacy of COSMO-RS for the scope of this project. Qualitative proof-of-concept experiments have been performed in a Parr bomb reactor at 40 °C and 1450 psi with various hold times. Solid Disperse Orange 1 has been successfully concentrated in situ to a generic IL (1-hexyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(triflouromethylsulfonyl)imide). The transfer of Disperse Orange 1 saturated in a generic ionic liquid to the same pure ionic liquid has also been successfully demonstrated in a proof of concept experiment. These experiments demonstrated transfer of a solute from both its pure solid form and saturated in a liquid. Selectivity has been demonstrated as well through the in situ concentration of a solid mixture of Disperse Orange 1 and Methylene Blue to a generic IL with the end result showing a higher affinity for Disperse Orange 1. Dyes have been used as model compounds due to the ease in which quantitative measurements can be taken through the use of UV-Vis spectroscopy.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: A Novel Hollow Fiber Membrane Embedded Co-Axial Microdevice for Simultaneous Extraction and Stripping
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Abstract The micro-chemical systems developed in the 1990s opened a new vision for chemical industry. The studies of micromixers, micro heat exchangers, micro reactors and micro dispersers have been comprehensively carried out. As for liquid-liquid extraction process, mass transfer distance and size of droplet are in the dimension of 10~1000 ¦Ìm in microdevices. In this characteristic dimension, the specific surface area can be more than 1000 times larger than the traditional extraction devices. Because of these advantages, microdisperion extraction has showed a brilliant application prospect in the purification of wet phosphoric acid, the separation of metal ions and organics, and the clean-up of alkaloids. Nevertheless, microdisperion extraction has its own limitation. In general, multistage process is necessary to realize higher recover ratio due to thermodynamic and phase ratio controls, and in microdevices this control can be more prominent. Therefore, how to achieve multistage process has become a frontier in microscale separation systems. In microchannels, the viscous force and interfacial tension replace the gravity and inertial forces as the dominant factors, which determines that the dispersion and flow regimes in microchannels are totally different from the traditional equipment. For example, the multistage countercurrent operation mode in extraction columns, which is driven by density difference between the two phases, cannot be performed in microchannels. In the 1960s, Li proposed the concept of liquid membrane permeation (LMP) and applied it to separation processes. According to the different configurations and modes of operation, LMP can be divided into two types, emulsion membrane (liquid surfactant membrane) and supported liquid membrane. The emulsion membrane involves three liquid phases, which can be respectively called external phase, internal phase and membrane phase. External phase and internal phase are separated by membrane phase by forming stable W/O/W or O/W/O double-emulsion system. Meanwhile, the membrane phase is also a bridge for transmission of solute from external phase to internal phase . In this way, the simultaneous extraction and stripping process is realized by transmission across the liquid membrane. Based on this concept, the membrane phase can be further absorbed in the micro pores of a porous support, which is called supported liquid membrane permeation. The liquid membrane formed on a support like hollow fiber membrane can be more stable than the emulsion membrane, and the specific surface area for mass transfer can also be increased. Based on the concept of LMP, realizing the dispersion and mass transfer process of liquid-liquid-liquid three phases in the same microdevice and coupling extraction and stripping to carry out multistage process are core contents of our study. We embedded a hollow fiber membrane in a microchannel to form the supported liquid membrane. Meanwhile, in order to solve the problem of high mass transfer resistance caused by the thickness of the membrane, we introduced a pressure control equipment to regulate the tube and shell pressures precisely and simultaneously, and in this way, the extractant could flow in the membrane pores oscillatorily to change the mass transfer process from original static state into convective flow state (see Fig. 1 ). As for the specific content of our study, we used the extraction of phenol as a model system, and realized the steady liquid-liquid-liquid three-phase flow of the feed, extractant, and back-extractant in the designed microdevice. By precisely controlling the pressure of the tube side, the extractant was separated from the feed in situ and passed into the shell side to contact with the back-extractant directly (see Fig. 2 ). In this way, both of the extraction yield and stripping yield reached 95%. And by introducing a transmembrane pressure with periodic oscillation, 5 theoretical stages were successfully achieved within 3 min residence time in the single microdevice. Hopefully, the method proposed in this study might bring a new idea for multistage microscale extraction processes. Fig. 1 . Simultaneous extraction and stripping process for separation of phenol in the microdevice 1 - pre-dispersion channel, 2 - hollow fiber membrane embedded channel , 3&4 - UV spectrophotometer 5&6 - buffer tank, 7 - pressure-control equipment, 8 - filter, 9 - valve, 10 - air tank Fig. 2 . Schematic diagram of experimental set-up

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Wnt-Notch Signaling Interactions during Neural and Glial Patterning of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Wnt-Notch Signaling Interactions during Neural and Glial Patterning of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Julie Bejoy 1 , Brent Bijonowski 1 , Teng Ma 1 , Yan Li 1,2 1 Department of Chemical and Biomedical Engineering; FAMU-FSU College of Engineering; Florida State University; Tallahassee, FL USA 2 Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, Florida State University, Tallahassee, Florida, USA Introduction: The human brain formation involves complicated processing which is regulated by a gene regulatory network involving different signaling pathways. The cross-regulatory interactions between elements of different pathways affect the process of cell fate assignment during neural and glial tissue patterning. In this study, the interactions between Wnt and Notch pathways, the two major pathways that influence neural and glial differentiation of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) individually, were investigated. In particular, the synergistic effects of Wnt-Notch pathway on the neural patterning processes along anterior-posterior (A-P) or dorsal-ventral (D-V) axis of hiPSC-derived cortical spheroids were explored. The human cortical spheroids derived from hiPSCs were treated with Wnt activator CHIR99021 (CHIR), Wnt inhibitor IWP4, Notch inhibitor (DAPT) individually, or in combinations (CHIR+DAPT, IWP4+DAPT). Materials and Methods: Human iPSK3 cells were seeded into Ultra-Low Attachment (ULA) 24-well plates. The formed EBs were treated with dual SMAD signaling inhibitors 10 μM SB431542 and 100 nM LDN193189. After 8 days, the cells were treated with fibroblast growth factor-2 and retinoic acid until day 16. During day 16-21, the spheroids were treated with six different conditions: (1) control, no small molecule was used; (2) CHIR99021 (10 μM), which activates Wnt signaling by inhibiting glycogen synthase kinase-3β; (3) IWP4, which inhibits Wnt signaling through the porcupine and thereby reducing the production of Wnt proteins; (4) the Notch inhibitor DAPT. The γ-secretase inhibitor DAPT can inhibit the γ-secretase dependent S3 cleavage of Notch, which releases the Notch internal cytoplasmic domain; (5) CHIR99021 plus DAPT (C+D); (6) IWP4 plus DAPT (I+D). To elucidate the influence of regional identity of neural progenitors on glial differentiation, the spheroids (day 21) of the six conditions were switched to BMP-4 treatment up to day 32. Results and Discussion: In our study, combinational treatments of Wnt and Notch modulators affected brain regional identity of iPSC-derived spheroids. The addition of DAPT to CHIR or IWP4 influences neural patterning effects of canonical Wnt pathway. Notch inhibition with DAPT reduced the hindbrain marker HOXB4, but the CHIR treatment was able to maintain HOXB4 expression in the presence of DAPT. Analysis of forebrain markers TBR1 and FOXG1 showed that IWP4 cannot maintain their expression in the presence of DAPT. I+D also reduced the expression of ventral forebrain marker Nkx2.1. The cortical spheroids that were treated with Wnt and Notch signaling modulators were then switched to gliogenesis by BMP4 treatment. The results showed that the CHIR group expressed the higher levels of astrocyte markers GFAP and Vimentin compared to the other groups. This might be because that CHIR treatment increased Notch activity and Notch ligand expression in the derived cortical spheroids. The lowest expression of astrocyte markers was shown in I+D group, indicating the dominance of DAPT treatment over IWP4 treatment on astrocyte differentiation and importance of Notch activation for astrogliogenesis. Conclusions: In this study, the functional cross-talk between Wnt and Notch signaling on neural and glial tissue patterning from hiPSCs were investigated using Wnt and Notch modulators. The results suggested the possibility of repressing effects of Notch inhibitor DAPT on Wnt inhibition and the positive impact of Wnt activation on Notch signaling for brain regional identity of hiPSC-derived cortical spheroids. Notch inhibition with DAPT reduced the hindbrain marker HOXB4, but CHIR was able to maintain HOXB4 expression in the presence of DAPT. Analysis of forebrain markers TBR1 and FOXG1 showed that IWP4 plus DAPT reduced forebrain marker expression. CHIR reduced the impact of DAPT on brain regional patterning whereas DAPT reduced Wnt inhibition effects. By switching the derived cortical spheroids to gliogenesis with BMP4, Wnt activator CHIR promoted the expression of astrocyte markers GFAP and Vimentin. The addition of Notch inhibitor DAPT to CHIR reduced astrocyte marker expression, confirming the importance of Notch activation on astrocyte generation. References Hayward, P., Kalmar, T., Arias, A.M., (2008) Wnt/Notch signaling and information processing during development. Development 135, 411-424. This study was supported by NSF CAREER (1652992) and NIH R03NS102640.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Amino Acid Coated Coated Gd2O3 Nanoparticles As a Potential T2 MRI-CT Dual Contrast Agents
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Gadolinium (Gd) is a unique and powerful element in chemistry and biomedicine which can be applied simultaneously to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and sensor. We report a facile method to synthesize Gd 2 O 3 nanoparticles for use as contrast agents in MRI. The nanoparticles were coated with ligand. The bonding status of ligand coated Gd 2 O 3 nanoparticles were confirmed by FT-IR and TGA. High voltage electron microscope (HVEM) shows that diacid coated (DA) coated Gd 2 O 3 nanoparticles were spherical in shape with an average diameter 3 mM. In addition, the bio-compatibility of the nanoparticles were measured by cytotoxicity tests by using human prostate cancer (DU145) and normal mouse hepatocyte (NCTC1469) cell lines which indicated that DA coated Gd 2 O 3 nanoparticles are not toxic up to 200 mM, making them a promising candidate for bio-medical applications. The high relaxivities provide an opportunity to conduct perfusion MRI experiments with significantly lower concentrations than those needed for current commercial agents.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Crude Oil Spot Sampling Methods and Their Impact on Thermophysical Properties
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: In many situations, spot sampling provides an economic means by which aliquots of crude oil can be captured from various points in the supply chain for composition, bubble point pressure, density, and sulfur content property analysis. However, inadvertent introduction of N 2 and other gases in sample handling systems during the sampling, transport, and analysis steps can cause difficulties when trying to assess the properties of the parent materials. These difficulties were investigated when compositions of crudes were measured via several analytical methods (ASTM D7169, ASTM D7900, ASTM D8003, GPA 2103, GPA 2177, GOR) on samples obtained from supply chains in North Dakota and Texas using a variety of spot sampling methods/containers (ASTM D3700, GPA 2174, ASTM D8009, ASTM 4057). The N 2 contents were compared to whole oil compositions derived from a tight-line flash gas compositional analysis paired with an Equation of State (EOS) model. The tight-line system was configured so that the pre-conditioning system and analytical equipment were connected directly to the oil process piping in the field. This minimized sample handling and potential for introducing air, and furthermore provided excess volume of oil to purge the pre-conditioning and analytical equipment with parent material. The whole oil compositions resulting from both the spot sampling and tight-line sample collection methods were used as input to a commercially available process simulator to calculate thermophysical properties. The prevalence of N 2 in the spot samples significantly changed calculated thermophysical properties, which can impact process models and classification of materials for transportation. The Crude Oil Characterization Research Study (funded by US DOE, DOT, and Transport Canada: http://energy.gov/fe/articles/crude-oil-characteristics-research , https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/archive/2018/02/the-great-crude-oil-fireball-test/552029/ ), seeks to understand the crude oil property differences between conventionally produced and tight oils. Recent activities analyzed the effects of sampling containers/techniques (ASTM D3700, GPA 2174, ASTM D8009, ASTM 4057) and sampling locations (Texas vs. North Dakota) on crude oil thermophysical property measurements. Different compositional measurement techniques (GPA 2103, GPA 2177, ASTM D7900, ASTM D7169, ASTM D8003, GOR flash) have been used to calculate these properties as well, providing insight into the features and limitations of these commercially available methodologies. https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: A Computationally Efficient Procedure for Studying Segregation in Alloy Materials with Monte Carlo Simulations
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: We present an advanced sampling technique based on Metropolis Monte Carlo (MC) to rapidly study phase behavior of several thousand - several million atoms alloy material systems at equilibrium. When the alloy material contains surfaces and preferential enrichment of one of constituent species at the top few surface layers is observed, the MC technique can be additionally used to study the surface segregation. In MC, starting with an initially random arrangement of the constituent atoms, equilibrium structures are attained by attempting trail moves, such as random displacements and swapping of randomly chosen pairs of atoms. However, the computational cost of MC simulations can become prohibitively high beyond a few thousand atoms and it may require several days to weeks of time to ultimately reach equilibrium. A simple idea is introduced to drastically reduce the computational cost by preparing the initial arrangement with the help of a nano thermodynamic model, which we have developed recently. The nano thermodynamic model is used to first estimate the composition of different surface and bulk regions of the material. The initial structure to be used in the MC calculation is prepared using the compositions that have estimated from the nano thermodynamic model so that the prepared structure is close to equilibrium. Using Au-Pt, Ni-Pt and Ag-Au as prototype systems, we demonstrate that a significant speed-up is achieved using our approach.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Modeling of Cation Exchange Membranes Using Maxwell-Stefan Approach for Chlor-Alkali System
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: The generalized Maxwell-Stefan approach is considered more suitable than the Nernst-Planck approach to describe multicomponent ion and water transport inside an ion exchange membrane. This is due to the fact that the Nernst-Planck approach is limited to dilute ionic systems due to the assumption of an ideal solution and neglection of ion-ion interactions [1, 2] , whereas many electrochemical processes involve highly concentrated and non-ideal solutions. The Maxwell-Stefan approach takes the interactions of different components and the non-ideal solutions into account. Moreover, the Maxwell-Stefan approach includes the water transport via the solvent-ion interactions whereas the Nernst-Planck model has to introduce a separate equation (i.e., the Schlögl equation) to account for the water transport [2, 3] . One main challenge in applying the Maxwell-Stefan approach is the lack of reliable data on diffusivities at high concentrations. Another weakness of a previously developed Maxwell-Stefan model [4] is the calculation of the membrane potential gradient by neglecting the concentration gradient and by using Ohm’s law to derive the potential gradient explicitly. The neutrality condition is broken by this simplification, which has been numerically proven during the investigation of the extended Nernst-Planck model [5] . In this presentation, we will show that semi-empirical correlations are suitable to define the Maxwell-Stefan diffusivities inside the membrane. T he newly developed model [6] has been used to predict transport numbers of ions and water for the chlor-alkali process and has been validated using the available experimental data (Figures 1a, 1b, and 2) . With the diffusivities presented in this work, the model shows a better fit to the experimental data than with previously reported fitted diffusivities [4, 7]. Figure 1. Also, we applied the Augmented matrix method [8] to solve both the concentration and the potential gradients simultaneously using the built-in partial differential equation parabolic elliptic (pdepe) solver in Matlab®. By adopting this method, no further assumption about the potential gradient is needed. The values of diffusivities also affect the membrane potential drop as shown in Figure 3. Our model shows a reasonable match with the experimental values of the membrane potential at 80 o C around 0.291 V at 3 kA.m -2 [9] and 0.51 V at 6 kA.m -2 [10] . This confirms the strong influence of the values of the Maxwell-Stefan diffusivities on the Maxwell-Stefan model. Figure 3. https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: Efficient Degradation of Imidacloprid through Biochar Activated Sodium Percarbonate
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Metal-free carbonaceous materials have been evaluated for the very first time to activate sodium percarbonate (SPC) for the degradation of insecticides. Palm empty fruit bunch biochar (PEFBB) was produced using pyrolyzation process. During this research work, a relatively low-cost carbonaceous material under limited oxygen supply for the activation of SPC to degrade imidacloprid was studied. The pyrolysis temperature was found to be a key parameter for the activation of SPC through biochar in the successive batch experiments. The degradation efficiency of imidacloprid considerably improved from 5.2 to 81.9 % when pyrolysis temperature increased from 250-850 o C. The degradation efficiency in the imidacloprid contaminated tap and ground water was 73.4 and 59.8% respectively. The elimination of excessive oxygen functional groups of biochar was found due to its higher temperatures, producing more defect structures with possible transformation and modulation of sp 3 carbons, thus enhancing the activation potential of biochar towards SPC. In addition, three intermediate products were identified and two different pathways were proposed as the major imidacloprid degradation. The reactive oxygen species (ROS) were studied using radical scavengers and electron spin resonance (ESR) to verify the dominant generation of hydroxyl radicals (OH ● ) in the biochar/SPC system. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR), Raman analysis and ESR combined X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) elucidated the generation of OH ● as well as superoxide (O 2 ●– ) free radicals due to the biochar defect structure. In conclusion, biochar activated SPC process is promising technique for the imidacloprid degradation that significantly enhance its application in the imidacloprid contaminated sites.

https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: Mass-Based Finite Volume Scheme for Aggregation, Growth and Nucleation Population Balance Equation Mehakpreet Singh a , Hamza Y. Ismail a , Themis Matsoukas b , Ahmad B. Albadarin a ,Gavin Walker a a Department of Chemical Science, Bernal Institute, University of Limerick, Ireland , e-mail: Mehakpreet.Singh@ul.ie b Department of Chemical Engineering, Pennsylvania State University, 158 Fenske Laboratory, University Park, USA Abstract This work is focused on developing new mass-based numerical method using the notion of Forestier and Mancini [1] for solving a one-dimensional aggregation population balance equation. The inherit issue of the existing finite volume schemes is that it required very fine grid for predicting the number density function accurately (Kumar et al. 2009). In addition to this, the sectional methods such as fixed pivot technique and cell average technique are computationally very expensive due to their complex formulations although highly accurate. It is observed that the existing numerical scheme does not predict the certain required moments of the number distribution functions accurately. In this present work, mass-based finite volume is developed which leads to the accurate prediction of different integral properties of number distribution functions. In order to check the accuracy and efficiency, the mass-based formulation is compared with the existing method for two kinds of benchmark kernels, namely, analytically solvable and practical oriented kernels. Moreover, the new mass-based and existed finite volume schemes are extended to solve a simultaneous aggregation-growth as well as aggregation-nucleation problems and are compared with the exact results. The comparison reveals that the mass-based numerical methods compute the number distribution functions as well as different order moments with higher precision by consuming less computational time than the existing method. Keywords : Particle, Aggregation, Growth, Nucleation, Population Balances, Finite volume Scheme. References : [1] Forestier- Coste , L., Mancini, S., 2012. https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.title: PAT-Facilitated Crystallization Development and Particle Engineering Via Mechanistic Understanding
https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/2019/meet.abstract: A development compound X which has a salt-formation step with a carboxylic acid was investigated to enhance understanding of its crystallization process. PAT Raman and FBRM were used to monitor the form transformation in real time and both were found to be indicative of the crystallization kinetics. A mechanistic model for solid form transformation was proposed based on the sequence of events involved and the mechanism was verified by the kinetic profiles revealed by Raman. A number of process variables were studied in a design of experiment (DoE) setting in order to identify the factors that impact the final attributes of the product such as particle size and morphology. The investigation, specifically through the precise quantitation by PAT, indicated the crystallization is primarily dictated by solvent composition and temperature. Other process variables such as seeds characteristics and acid addition rate were also evaluated and their effects on the outcome were found to be secondary. This insight helped steer the focus of development efforts to enhance the robustness of the process. A quantitative prediction model on particle size was extracted from the array of experiments and its accuracy was demonstrated at various spots of the parameter range covered by the study.
